CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

This is what I did as a previous customer and now a internal employee here at Zscaler.

In a very large organization it became very apparent, very quickly with Cloud Sandbox that Per SaaS service rules may become to cumbersome so here is what I did.

This was done with full Governance, Risk and Compliance department approval  within a large research, education, and practical Healthcare environment,

We take the Document Type ---- which is broken into very  specific categories -----  and set a single rule to Type + a custom URL category ----that matches ---- and only the approved Destination URLs are added to the Custom category and the Rule Action --- becomes Allow and Scan  --- with subsequent to BLOCK

this creates like less then 10 full rules maybe depending how you break them up

We did not have Mobile so that was skipped ( big, huge, massive IOS shop)

So it looks like this

Rule Name   --- Allow   Archive  --- URL custom category --- Allow Archive

Rule Name --- Allow Executable --- URL custom category ---  All exe

Rule Name ---- Allow PDF (aka Other docs) ---- URL custom category -- Allow PDF

Rule Name ---- Allow MS Office ----------- URL custom category --- Allow MS OFFICE

Rule Allow --- Archive & EXE

Rule Allow MS Office & PDF  <---- most popular

Rule Allow MS Office & PDF & EXE <----- 2nd for use and total URLs

Rule Allow DevOPS ------ this was the single catch all they need all categories ---  URL custom cat --- Allow DevOps  <-- reviewed monthly --- this was also locked down by AD security group for a Users --  when I left this had 3 website in it and that was it

It is dependent on the Zscaler (IA) admin team to  ensure that Categories are not Nested and URLs only show up in one place the most specific rule wins and if that means you move a URL from one custom category tot he next so be it.

So simple, concise relatively easy to manage --- we at Zscaler could work on the Description field for more space but it was hyper function al and easy for Auditors, Admins, Support, etc

CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

Past that leave the Default rule at the bottom and add categories to it if needed but again that is a maturity aspect and each customer will be different as RISK appetite and acceptance vary greatly

CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

I would also recommend enabling AI verdict for testing as that is a new feature that is really good --- AI used to be only enabled if first action was Quarantine --- now it is either Allow and Scan or Quarantine

## If I upload a file for Sandbox behavioral analysis, does it always get detonated?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evn6JCAQ/if-i-upload-a-file-for-sandbox-behavioral-analysis-does-it-always-get-detonated
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T09:29:58.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

awl

(Employee) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

September 11, 2017 at 9:31 PM

If I upload a file for Sandbox behavioral analysis, does it always get detonated?

I’m just wondering if I upload a file to the Sandbox, does it always get detonated in the cloud sandbox?

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

1 answer

481 views

Top Rated Answers

Jozef_Krakora

(Employee)

9 years ago

In short, no. In some cases, a file that is uploaded via

http://filecheck.zscaler.com/

is not actually detonated in the Cloud Sandbox.

The file sample must be no greater than 20 MB in size in order for it to be analyzed in Sandbox.

The file must be uploaded from a network and organization that is a paying customer of Cloud Sandbox subscription.

The file must not be blocked by anti-virus or other Zscaler Advanced Threat Protection security inspection layers. If it is, the file sample will not “reach? the Sandbox.

The file must be of a supported file type.

Last, but not least, the file must also not already have a Sandbox verdict. It the file has already been detonated in the Cloud Sandbox, and has a Sandbox verdict and detail behavioral analysis report available, it will not be submitted to the Sandbox for re-detonation.

See this help article for more on the basic use of the Sandbox Scanning Portal:

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/204362839-How-do-I-upload-files-to-the-Sandbox-Scanning-Portal-

See this help article for more on how to view the detail Sandbox behavioral analysis report:

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/216226163

See this help article for more on the Sandbox Scanning Portal results:

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/214369226

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/204362839-How-do-I-upload-files-to-the-Sandbox-Scanning-Portal-

See this help article for more on how to view the detail Sandbox behavioral analysis report:

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/216226163

See this help article for more on the Sandbox Scanning Portal results:

https://support.zscaler.com/hc/en-us/articles/214369226

## What does the "other" URL category mean?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evn6LCAQ/what-does-the-other-url-category-mean
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T09:30:00.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

awl

(Employee) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

September 11, 2017 at 8:22 PM

What does the "other" URL category mean?

What should we expect to show up in the “other? category?

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

1 answer

372 views

Top Rated Answers

chandan

(Employee)

9 years ago

There are several types of “Other? URL categories included in the Zscaler solution. Zscaler uses 6 different classes of URL Categories that are further broken down into 28 different types of Super Categories.

These Super Categories are further broken down into specific Categories and when a URL belongs to a Super Category but not to a specific Category underneath it, it is placed in the “Other? category of the Super Category.

This 100% works in Zscaler — however you may need to set up a couple Firewall rules for your external / internal systems as seen on the clients — as the network design and delivery method to Zscaler is critical here ----- ON site Location based policies for IPsec / GRE — probably need the least care and feeding as you shouldn’t need to proxy UCaaS traffic and voice/shared video etc … from enterprisee systems typically would not get proxied and mgmt style FTP or DHCP option 56 used to set the back end mgmt /call / configuration servers would typically be internal downloads and why proxy it out just to bring it right back in ----- However Zscaler Client Connector ---- running Tunnel Forwarding 2.0 – for full DTLS 2.0 all ports all protocols ---- that is where the FW rule may need to be applied — as two rules – one for SSO, config, updates, etc — and the other for adherence specific to voice and collaboration and Video aspects. Jabber needs to inquiry the Internet DNS for _collab-edge SRV to expressway, but Finesse will inquiry Internal DNS to reach out the internal Cisco UCCX server. how to setup it?

hfregoso

(Employee)

5 years ago

You don’t really need to bypass all the IPs. It is based on the SRV records that your Cisco Finesse and Jabber use. Place a packet capture with Zscaler off.

You will see a DNS request to two SRV records.

_cisco-uds._tcp.safemarch.com

_cuplogin._tcp.safemarch.com

If Jabber doesnt see a DNS response for the first and second SRV it will try the one below:

_collab-edge._tls.safemarch.com

Your DNS will response most likely with another FQDN and TCP port which normally is 443.

Lets say the response was FQDN with .safemarch.com domain something like

voice.safemarch.com

then you will need to bypass this last one.

In ZPA create an app segment an include the 1st, 2nd SRV and the DNS response as a result of the third query.

This is what you need to bypass:

_cisco-uds._tcp.safemarch.com

_cuplogin._tcp.safemarch.com

voice.safemarch.com

Use all ports in your bypass

This will make your traffic go over ZIA only traffic destined for

voice.safemarch.com

If you want to exclude that traffic out of ZIA now you only need bypass that traffic. Use any known bypass method for ZIA.

I hope this helps and good luck with your project.

## China and ZIA PAC

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnDVCAY/china-and-zia-pac
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:47:29.000Z

russkil

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

July 22, 2021 at 4:05 PM

China and ZIA PAC

Trying to get to a Zscaler PAC File that will work in china with Office 365, anyone got any good pointers to what to create?

One question that comes to mind should all traffic go via a ZScaler DC and none go direct to help with giving better connectivity?

Client Connector

8 answers

1.1K views

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

4 years ago

the ‘_FX’-suffix dynamically issues gateway IP addresses based on the client fingerprints, i.e. all users coming from a single egress IP address are given an IP address from a pool of healthy gateway IP addresses. The fingerprint is used to ensure that a single device continues its session to the same gateway IP address.

Alternatively you could use ‘_F0’-’_F7’ to distribute your users across multiple gateway IPs based on your own logic.

Without any of these suffixes all your clients (coming in via the same egress IP) end up on the same gateway IP.

Hello,

I wanted to make a query to see if you can help me, as it is a topic that generates many doubts.

In our organization we are considering to replace the Physical Proxy with the ZIA zscaler solution. Currently some internal servers of our organization that navigate to the Internet through the Physical Proxy, need to be presented with a specific public Ip of our organization, since at the other end the servers to which they connect (almost all applications based on HTTPS) are configured in their Whitelist firewalls and only allow us access to the service when the Ip of Origin is a specific one.

Is there any functionality in ZIA that allows this or should we continue with a physical proxy and continue using it for this type of traffic? I understand that if there is a solution, Zscaler would take control of our public addressing?

Thank you very much.

Client Connector

forum, although it may be more appropriate for the ZIA forum. The SIPA solution doesn’t require the Client Connector to operate, and servers can take advantage of SIPA using the destination as the criteria (e.g. if servers are accessing

Alvaro - the Source IP Anchoring (SIPA) capability in ZIA is something that can be deployed to address this concern. More information about SIPA can be found here:

Source IP Anchoring

Please note, to continue using the same egress IP address(es) you use today, the connector (a virtual image) can be installed at the same location as your current physical proxy. The cloud location depicted in the diagram is the most advantageous from a network path perspective given the applications requiring a static IP are on the public Internet but it also requires you to re-register the egress IP assigned to you in the public cloud of your choice with the applications that require a specific public IP.

## When "allow due to insufficient app data" log entry value appears and when it does not

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnDdCAI/when-allow-due-to-insufficient-app-data-log-entry-value-appears-and-when-it-does-not
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-12-09T15:00:35.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Stefan Sebastian

(Employee) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

Edited December 9, 2024 at 3:00 PM

When "allow due to insufficient app data" log entry value appears and when it does not

The log entry will NOT appear if the DPI simply failed to detect the application

The Admin will NOT see the “Allow due to insufficient app data" indication under the “Action" column in the logs if the DPI (network application) failed to detect after 12 packets.

If the network application wasn’t detected after 12 packets then the Advanced Cloud Firewall (ACFW) will try to match on the “leaf" data already assembled: so TCP + SSL/TLS + HTTPS for example when a complete leaf might look like TCP + SSL/TLS + HTTPS + Salesforce (with Salesforce as the network app in this example). If there was a rule for either TCP or SSL/TLS or HTTPS then that indication will be given in the logs instead.

The conditions when the log entry appears:

The Admin will only see the “Allow due to insufficient app data" indication under the “Action" column in the logs if the session was terminated gracefully or suddenly before the network application identification process could finish. The network application identification process occurs on or before the 12th packet but mostly between packets 2 to 5 and as counted from those sent from the user /session-initiator perspective.

Getting the “Allow due to insufficient app data" indication assumes the ACFW rule was ranked appropriately versus other possible ACFW rules so that TCP and then SSL/TLS and then HTTPS were not blocked prior to the rule with the Salesforce application identification failure. It is these few (more than 1 but less than 13) packets associated to the precursor identification “leaves" that was the

allowed

traffic referenced by “allow due to insufficient app data".

As distinct from network applications, network services are just protocol (TCP, UDP) + dest:port and so always match on the first packet. The user will never see an “Allow due to insufficient app data?? message because of a network service condition in a CFW rule.

Network Application usage best practices

The use of network applications in Advanced CFW rules is a tradeoff between certainty (network applications are the highest confidence identifications) and delay (can identify as late as the 12th packet of any given flow or not at all).

When a rule has a network application, then all qualifying flows will potentially match the rule until the network application is identified and the condition is either true or false. It is therefore recommended that whenever possible:

If the network application is part of a higher ordered rule then blend the network application condition with at least one other condition that makes the rule “qualify" to a very limited number of sessions/flows. For example, add a destination IP address to the rule so the DPI engine only tries to identify network apps destined to that IP (as a logical “AND" condition). Add a user condition, add a network services condition, etc. The more conditions the more specific the DPI identification is applied;

If network applications are the only condition in the firewall rule then order the rule lower than rules where a first packet identifications are possible (in particular below rules where block actions occur since this traffic is never wanted). This allows for those higher ordered rules to match and take their configured action and only a subset of all flows remain for examination as part of the network application DPI identification.

Please see

Best Practice for CFW Rules with Network Application Detections as Conditions

for more information

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

## Sandboxed files not downloading

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnEnCAI/sandboxed-files-not-downloading
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-05-31T08:52:21.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

tony_odonnell

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

June 20, 2019 at 3:59 PM

Sandboxed files not downloading

Anyone else having issues with the Sandbox where files don’t download?

It seems to be guaranteed to fail if downloading a number of individual files from Wetransfer as a zip.

It takes just over 10 minutes before finally getting redirected back to Wetransfer at which point their dynamic link has timed out and the file is no longer available.

Similar issues experienced with files hosted on AWS.

It seems that the main problem is that the sandbox service is just too slow.

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

2 answers

1.24K views

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

7 years ago

I would suggest you look at “Allow and scan? instead of “Quarantine?.

We have a very strict policy where we want to Quarantine everything.

We use a Custom URL Category to define which URLs hit the allow and scan policy if they behave in the way you are suggesting.

Jozef_Krakora

(Employee)

7 years ago

Hi Tony,

There are a few ways to manage how a file download attempt is treated when it is also being analyzed by Zscaler Cloud Sandbox. Have you reached out to Zscaler Support via

https://help.zscaler.com/submit-ticket

on this case yet? If not, I would encourage that as they would be best equipped to troubleshoot the cases you have experienced and provide feedback on how to optimize your policy.

In short though, a file is generally analyzed by Cloud Sandbox only if it has never been seen before, has passed other security engines already without a clear verdict, and only if it is suspicious in nature. In your case, it seems that the file was temporarily quarantined, and after that, the dynamic link had expired. If that is the case, the user may need to re-authenticate the download request. If it is the same file, it will not be held a second time, and should be available for download, assuming it was not found malicious.

It is also possible to set granular policy on how to treat files that are being analyzed in Sandbox for the first time. Read more here

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-sandbox-policy

for the “First-Time Action?. Let us know if this helps.

Jozef K

Hi tshaughnessy,

I wanted to access your document but seems it's no longer available. Can you please share it again? I'm looking for a way to block contents on websites and not the whole website. Any information in this regard is appreciated.

Jerry P. Gurrea

(Customer)

8 months ago

Found this article in the support portal that you can explore.

Create Custom URL Categories:

In the Zscaler Admin Portal, go to

Administration > URL Categories

and add a new custom category. List the URLs for the specific YouTube videos or channels you want to allow (e.g.,

youtube.com/channel/<ChannelID>

or

www.youtube.com/watch?v=<VideoID>

Create a URL Category to Block the Rest of YouTube:

Add another custom category with broader YouTube URLs (e.g., .

youtube.com

, .

googlevideo.com

, etc.) to block general access.

Configure URL Filtering Rules:

Go to

Policy > URL & Cloud App Control

and create rules:

Allow access to the custom category for specific videos/channels.

Block access to the category covering the rest of YouTube.

Use Tenant Profiles for Channel/Category Control:

For more granular control, create a

Tenant Profile

and specify allowed YouTube Channel IDs or Category IDs. Apply this profile in your Cloud App Control policy.

Validate the Policy:

Test by accessing the allowed video/channel and confirm that other YouTube content is blocked.

SSL Inspection is not being enforced, but under SSL Inspection settings, the category is blocked.

skottieb

(Employee)

Hi Mark,

Today we do not log the rule name/type for allowed traffic as there are many policy and security items that can ‘allow’ the traffic, as this is allowed traffic, its why you are seeing None in the rule name.

As for why the traffic is being allowed when you intent is to block, this could be for a number of reasons, including the lack of SSL inspection. Our support team is best positioned to help you with this, they can work with you on tracing why the traffic is allowed and recommending the best policy construct. So you have an ticket open for the same issue?

Cheers,

@skottieb

## Standard vs Advance Firewall Feature Clarification

- Type: Q&A

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

snaveen

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

April 29, 2019 at 4:03 AM

Standard vs Advance Firewall Feature Clarification

Dear All,

As i understood, for DNS security and controls will required advanced Cloud firewall license.Can you please suggest following Cloud IPS features included in the standard firewall? or required Advance Cloud Firewall? Thank you in advance!

Cloud IPS

• Delivers always-on IPS threat protection and coverage,

regardless of user connection or location

• Inspects all user traffic on and off network, to restore full

visibility into user, app, and internet connections

regards,

Naveen

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

1 answer

1.06K views

Top Rated Answers

skottieb

(Employee)

7 years ago

Hi Naveen,

Thanks for your question. Cloud IPS is part of Advanced Cloud Firewall.

Please note that signature/IPS based protections for Proxy (Web/FTP) are included of the Business Bundle as per the current packaging. Advanced Cloud Firewall is part of the Transformation Bundle which includes Cloud IPS for other (non web/FTP) applications.

Cheers,

Scott-

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

June 1, 2023 at 4:33 PM

All Windows profiles see the same Zscaler user logged

Hello Zenith Community,

I face to a particular case that it doesn’t work as expected, and needs to fix it.

In this company some computers are shared and can be used by multiple users. Some users have Zscaler access to browse intranet/internet, some users have not any Zscaler access and can only browse intranet.

When a user with internet access logon to Windows, access to internet from Edge or Chrome and log off, Zscaler seems stills logged to user with internet access. If another user without any Zscaler access logon to Windows and types

https://ip.zscaler.com

from the browser, he will see the user with internet access stills logged to Zscaler. It should definitively not, but it is what happens in my case.

My problem

If a user without any Zscaler access logon to Windows and disable cookies option into Edge or Chrome, then he is able to browse internet without any restriction while he has not access to browse internet.

edge://settings/content/cookies > Allow sites to save and read cokies data (recommended) > Disabled

chrome://settings/cookies > Block all cookies (not recommended) > Selected

Can someone help me to figure out a way to fix this issue?

Best regards,

Raphaël

How do you forward traffic to Zscaler? Using a proxy setting/Pac file or using Zscaler Client Connector. For a machine with multiple sessions I would advise you to use Proxy setting/PAC file.

Maybe that coming to the feature IP surrogate that seems enabled to our users, but I do not find any reference about this behavior.

Or maybe I'm wrong, and this behavior linked to another option that I did not identified yet.

Raphael

Just to provide an update on this topic, because we identified the root cause.

Issue coming to the IP Surrogate feature.

## Location-Based Policy for Road Warriors

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykCACAY/locationbased-policy-for-road-warriors
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-02T17:16:09.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Naith

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

May 2, 2023 at 3:42 PM

Location-Based Policy for Road Warriors

I work for a company with no Customer location and only Road Warriors.

Is there any way to have location-based policies set for remote users?

There is not GRE or IPSec Configured. Only PAC files and Client Connector on managed devices.

At RSA, one of the sales team mentioned it was in the pipelines or is already available.

TIA,

ZIA - Forwarding

5 answers

4.43K views

Grizzly

(Customer)

3 years ago

I am kind of in the same boat.

No GRE or IPSEC only Pac and ZCC (more than 2/3s of work force is remote, and road warrior). I am running into issues with south TX users going through Mexican datacenters, but some USA based websites are blocking access from Mexico.

Is there a way to force USA based users to use USA based DC’s?

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

did you already try

country gw variables?

Andreas

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi,

since you have “no location”, what is your use case for a location based policy?

Is it like:

If user is in United States: allow URL Category “Vehicle” outside of US block it.

Enable SSL Inspection only in Country X

CU

Andreas

Naith

(Customer)

3 years ago

Yes, so based on the location, different policies applies. So If User is in EMEA or China…different policies apply.

Andreas

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi,

that is interesting.

If your locations have static IP addresses than you can assign the particular IP address to a location. This should work also without GRE or IPSec. You can do so and check the logs if location is recognized correctly. It worked for me for testing when working from home as my ISP rarely changes the IP address. However, this will not work for normal road warriors.

The only other thing that comes to my mind is to use the IDP. I think Azure can identify the origin of an request (in order to recognize “impossible travel attack”).

Perhaps it can apply ad-hoc a group attribute with the country of origin. (I have no idea if any IDP is capable of doing so.)

In that case you could use such group in a policy.

However it would also require either SCIM / Authentication bridge (in order to update the Zscaler UserDB ad-hoc) or the user has to logout/login each time he travels from one location to a location with a different ruleset.

Also, if users are quite static an do not travel often, you can assign a permanent country group to them.

Of course than Country A policy still applies, if user is in Country B.

Worst case solution: Update the business travel process. A user that needs to travel also needs to apply for a change of his IDP country group.

I hope you are not working for an airline that needs the pilots to use Zscaler.

CU

andreas

(Partner) to

(Employee): asked a question.

May 23, 2023 at 10:30 AM

Traffic from Bloomberg application doesn't reach ZIA

One of my customers have Bloomberg application. We have configured ZIA to allow custom ports and IPs listed in the document. In addition we also have SIPA configuration, because Bloomberg only allows certain IP addresses.

G-Man, I've started looking at the ZIA Posture Profiles to see how we can leverage this.  I've created a ZIA posture with multiple trust levels and it seems to identify systems quite well.  We aren't using them in any policies today, but it gives a good idea of which systems are High, Medium, Low and Unknown (ie: BYOD)

You can export the enrolled devices and filter on the trust levels.

Examples:

High Trust - domain joined, AV check, FW check , cert, reg key, etc.

Med Trust - domain joined, AV check, FW check

Low Trust - domain joined

Unknown - this will be BYOD devices that meet no device posture check

About the Enforcement Points category

The Enforcement Points category is dedicated to enforcement policy discussions. Such as inline web, inline email, out of band for SaaS apps , and at the endpoint

Enforcement Points

1 answer

503 views

AgarciaZ34691

(Employee)

3 days ago

Hello,

Please also find the next documentation which could be helpful:

Use the right enforcement point:

Inline Web DLP for traffic in transit at the gateway.

Outbound Email DLP for SMTP-bound mail (subject, body, attachments).

SaaS Security API DLP (out-of-band) for files/messages in sanctioned SaaS apps.

Endpoint DLP for device channels (printing, removable storage, network share, clipboard, app file access).

Docs:

Inline Web DLP (configure rules):

Configuring DLP Policy Rules with Content Inspection

Outbound Email DLP overview:

What Is Zscaler Outbound Email DLP?

SaaS Security API DLP policy:

Configuring the SaaS Security API DLP Policy

About Data at Rest Scanning DLP

Endpoint DLP (configure rules):

Configuring Endpoint DLP Policy Rules

Build detection logic once, reuse across points:

About DLP Engines

Hi ya,

This is the OP using a different login. The answer is kind of complicated and not great. So yes you can do inline DLP on the Outlook web client if you drop back to the old one click config, but it isn't very good. You have no ability to use the email recipient in your ruleset so you can't allow a certain file to be able to sent to person A but not person B. And if it's blocked users get a generic error message so they have no idea what just happened.

And support never got it working at all for the outlook desktop client. That may have changed now.

## Need help with changing proxy mode to transparent for Linux

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykQ6CAI/need-help-with-changing-proxy-mode-to-transparent-for-linux
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-02T17:15:54.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

shivam.chouksey

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

April 4, 2023 at 10:27 AM

Need help with changing proxy mode to transparent for Linux

Hello Team,

We are using explicit proxy on our Linux infrastructure. The proxy settings are defined as specific Zscaler nodes i.e.

man1.sme.zscloud.com

or Lon3.x.x.x. There have been multiple issues over time using these proxy settings and Zscaler has recommended to move to transparent mode. We are looking for the guidance on how best this change can be implemented without risk to the business. What configuration changes will be required at network/infra level? Any guidance will be helpful and appreciated.

Thanks

Shivam

ZIA - Forwarding

6 answers

914 views

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

in a nutshell:

Built a IPSec/GRE tunnel in between the linux machines location and Zscaler (eg on your router) and then (if the tunnel device is not your default GW anyways) route traffic from that linux machine towards ‘anything internet’ through that device

shivam.chouksey

(Partner)

3 years ago

Thanks Thomas for your reply

I have a few follow up questions please

The servers have the explicit proxy defined. Do we need to remove it to force the traffic through the tunnel?

The server traffic is going out through the DC firewalls, so the tunnels should be created between FW device and the Zscaler?

What is the ‘Tunnel device’ you are referring to?

Kind regards

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

you don’t need to remove the proxy settings.

Even if they are still set (say to man1) and you have a tunnel to was1 then the was1 proxies would pick them up and process.

If you send traffic through your FW already and that FW can establish a IPSec tunnel to ZS then you just need to assure that traffic towards internet is then sent into that tunnel and no longer directly to internet.

For testing i’d propose that you start with sending ONLY traffic from that linux server into the tunnel and have all other devices accessing internet directly.

shivam.chouksey

(Partner)

3 years ago

Thomas:

just need to assure that traffic towards internet is then sent into that tunnel and no longer directly to internet.

Thank you again Thomas.

Please don’t mind my silly questions but could you please elaborate on how I can achieve this?

“just need to assure that traffic towards internet is then sent into that tunnel and no longer directly to internet.”

Thomas Scharl

(Customer)

3 years ago

in our case we did pretty much the same as what you are trying now.

What we did was to setup a PBR aka ‘policy based routing’ on our network infra (L3 core swtich) which sends traffic from the internal server over to the device (in our case a dedicated router) which has the tunnel towards ZScaler CENR.

In your case what you need is as far as i see a PBR on your firewall which acts like ‘if source IP=IP-linux-.server THEN send trafifc into tunnel, if soruce IP is anything else → do NOT send into tunnel’.

With that only the linux servers traffic would get sent to ZScaler while anything else works exactly as it does right now.

shivam.chouksey

(Partner)

3 years ago

Thank you so much Thomas for your detailed response. Let me check this solution internally and come back to you in case of further queries.

Have a great day.!

## ZScaler firewall traffic allowed due to insufficient app data

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykQJCAY/zscaler-firewall-traffic-allowed-due-to-insufficient-app-data
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-02T17:16:47.000Z

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

avshch

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 30, 2023 at 1:34 PM

ZScaler firewall traffic allowed due to insufficient app data

Hello,

We have some traffic which is allowed through ZScaler Cloud Firewall with “Allow due to insufficient app data”. Is there a way to block this kind of traffic?

Thanks,

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Discourse-expand

Far-image

7 answers

2.29K views

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

3 years ago

This is part of the deep packet inspection that Zscaler does. It will allow up to 12 packets to try and determine the application before it closes the connection. This happens on the first firewall rule that has a network application defined.

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

3 years ago

About Network Applications | Zscaler

avshch

(Customer)

3 years ago

@GordonWright

So what happens after it is not able to determine the application? Does it block access? If so how can the log entries could be corelated? Thanks,

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

3 years ago

It then applies policy based on network port. So if you don’t allow that port it will be blocked.

avshch

(Customer)

3 years ago

image

Gordon Wright

(Customer)

3 years ago

It might do if you are using some kind of authenticated user to allow or block in the policy,

the sub-location defined is an IP addresses of an appliance (PaloAlto firewall) accessing update url’s. It can not support SAML-based authentication. On the location level we require authentication as a fail-safe for any unknown IP addresses within the IP range of the location.

## Bing ChatGPT feature is not working through Zscaler

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykQLCAY/bing-chatgpt-feature-is-not-working-through-zscaler
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-05T04:51:35.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - SSL Inspection

SMenchinger

(Partner) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

March 29, 2023 at 3:45 PM

Bing ChatGPT feature is not working through Zscaler

Bing has recently rolled out a new AI feature with ChatGPT. This feature is accessible when using the “Bing Discover” plug-in that comes with Microsoft Edge. When using ZIA with full SSL inspection, you can expect the “Bing Discover” plug-in to display an error message.

image

441×848 13.5 KB

To resolve this issue, follow the steps below:

Open your ZIA admin portal and navigate to Policy > SSL Inspection

Click “Add an SSL Inspection Rule”. Click the drop down on “URL Categories” and click the + icon to add a new URL Category. NOTE: Ensure this rule is above any “SSL inspect all traffic” rules.

22

773×705 34.3 KB

Give your new URL category a name and add “.bing.com” to the Custom URL or URLs retaining parent category and save this URL category.

33

702×901 40.1 KB

Lastly, scroll down to the bottom of the new SSL inspection rule and set the action to “Do Not Inspect” > “Bypass Other Policies”. Save this SSL Inspection rule and activate the change on the left.

44

733×507 15.3 KB

Exit out of your Edge browser completely and re-open the browser. Your Bing discover plug-in should now work along with the AI chat feature.

ZIA - SSL Inspection

Armando

Hi @Sam Menchinger​ usually when there are features that do not work with Zscaler we need to take a HAR file while reproducing the issue to see all the URLs in question.

Once we have that info, we can go to the web insights to look for inconsistencies, such as:

Are all the URLs subject to SSL inspection?

Are all the URLs in question are being allowed?

Do we see any errors such as client/server handshake failures?

Is this happening for all users and machines or just from 1 specific location?

With the above, we'll have a good starting point to start troubleshooting these type of issues.

Thanks.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

3 years ago

thedman27:

Undetectable Fil

this may help you

File Types

: Select file types to which you want to apply the rule. You can also select

Undetectable File

under

Other

to apply the rule to unknown file types. For unknown file types, the service checks for the file type in the file header using true file type detection. If the file is still unknown, the service performs MIME type checks and tags as an unknown file type for any that fall outside of well-defined MIME types for common apps. You can select any number of file types and also search for file types.

## ZScaler Packet Capture npcap Network Traffic

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009eykY9CAI/zscaler-packet-capture-npcap-network-traffic
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-10-31T01:00:24.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

JPengu

(Customer) to

sfdc

(Employee): asked a question.

May 12, 2023 at 1:42 PM

ZScaler Packet Capture npcap Network Traffic

Does ZScaler’s packet capture w/npcap alter the flow of network traffic to/from your system?

The reason why I ask is because our company is running into issues where Office365 is unable to reach the licensing server to reactivate the client and when starting packet capture with ZScaler the license goes through and Office activates itself (Office only looks for activation every 30 days), so this issue is being difficult to troubleshoot because our troubleshooting/investigation steps are resolving the issue and after 30 days the issue returns because packet capture isn’t continuously running.

Ps. This is only affecting Office products. Every other application/network path seems to be running fine. I would greatly appreciate any answers on this one.

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

3 answers

1.2K views

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Jonathan P Wilson​ The packet capture feature does not alter or modify the network traffic flow in any way. Any changes you may have observed are likely coincidental, as enabling or disabling packet capture shouldn't impact the network path—it will remain unchanged regardless.

kartikay.mishra

(Partner)

9 months ago

Ideally there is no link for pcap and O365 licence server connectivity issue. very sure start the pcap and trying to connect with re-login in O365 and get the licnese server in case disconnection surely you will get the logs in Pcap.

JPengu

(Customer)

9 months ago

This was not coincidental. I would click on the license activation button - in O365 Classic - and would attempt this 5 times and would fail to acquire the license all 5 times. As soon as I would enable packet capture, the license would go through. This issue existed for a long time and I personally saw the results 134 times, on 134 different workstations (I used to be technical support during this issue and counted the tickets).

Once I found the workaround I shared it with my coworkers. There were 1,086 resolved tickets in total. I can assume that this method worked 1,086 times on 1,086 different workstations with 100% resolution (w/5% deviation).

Turned out the installation of npcap was opening a port for that traffic to go through (npcap installs automatically when running packet capture). Just needed to track down what port/s it was opening.

Bhisham

(Customer) asked a question.

June 8, 2023 at 6:23 PM

ZIA with Full Tunnel VPN

We have couple of MAC users who work for client, and they use client provided full tunnel VPN so once we have installed the ZCC on them and now ZCC traffic is via the VPN their couple of URL's stops working. how we can resolve such issue on MAC?

ZIA - Forwarding

1 answer

442 views

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Bhisham Sharma​ In this case, we would need to know the URL that stopped working and also compare if this works in Windows clients for instance.

If this works in Windows users, we may need to check the App Profile and forwarding profile that we have in Windows vs the ones that we have in MAC.

Those are the main differences as we need different App profiles for MAC users as for Windows, so that's going to be our starting point.

If no major differences, we'll need to look further, is SSL inspection enabled? Does the Server support/allow proxy connections? Do we see the traffic in the web insights?

Based on the above, we should be able to develop a solid action plan.

Thanks.

akita_down

For anyone looking for a solution to this.... You can make the URL Search appear after going through different reports. Definitely something that needs to be fixed.

You'll need to go into "Analytics | Web Insights"

Select your timeframe that you are searching within

Then change the "Overall Traffic" dropdown to "Domain" - once that loads, click on the top result and select "User" - This is the only way to make the "URL Search" filter appear in this view.

Once that finishes loading, you can change the "URL Search" Filter to whatever website you're looking for.

## DLP for Capturing GenerativeAI Logs

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009iZIxwCAG/dlp-for-capturing-generativeai-logs
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-30T16:14:51.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Policy Rules

curiouscreature89

(Customer) asked a question.

June 22, 2023 at 4:47 PM

DLP for Capturing GenerativeAI Logs

Hi Team,

We want to create the DLP rules to capture the GenerativeAI logs e.g., if a user access CHATGPT or any other websites and search for any company related information on it. It should create a incident and generate the logs.

Could anyone guide us to achieve this using Zscaler DLP?

Policy Rules

2 answers

716 views

twikel

(Employee)

3 years ago

When determining to build a rule whether it's based off a URL classification or an application you can perform a URL lookup with inside the Zscaler console. Below is an example of looking up the ChatGPT main URL.

In Zscaler DLP you can do a DLP rule with and without content inspection. To capture the traffic posting to ChatGPT a DLP rule without content inspection needs to be created. A rule without content inspection won't look for specific DLP content, instead it'll look for everything posted to that application for example. In the example below is a rule that is specifically looking at ChatGPT as an application. As an action we have set it to allow and for all DLP incidents to be sent to the Zscaler incident receiver for further review.

When enabling a rule like this it must be remember that everything going to that application specifically in the example above will be captured. So to help reduce the amount of un-needed incidents we can exclude specific URLs specific to this website that are not inclusive to the chat transfer. These URLs may include the list below. However it is always important to perform testing to ensure that the destination application hasn't made changes since the time of this writing. This can be performed per URL or a custom URL category can be utilized to streamline this bypass process.

chat.openai.com/cdn-cgi/challenge-platform

chat.openai.com/backend-api/conversation/gen_title

chat.openai.com/api/auth/signin/

chat.openai.com/backend-api/moderations

1 like

tc_zs

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi

@curiouscreature89

(Customer)

​  - I've got this working in our environment.

Created a DLP Dictionary - with the pattern match of

"input":".*","model"

Tied this to a DLP Engine (match the epxression > 0)

Then created a DLP policy rule for the ChatGPT Cloud Application

So we get an alert each time someone posts a query to ChatGPT - the question asked is captured by the regex (its not perfect - but found it hard to work with the limitations on the Zscaler side, so likely could be refined further).  The full content is also captured in the attachment.

I also have similar working for Bard - this uses the pattern match of

null,".*\",0,null

Hope this helps!

## Configuring an IPSec Tunnel in RouterOS (Mikrotik Router)

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009iZzWICA0/configuring-an-ipsec-tunnel-in-routeros-mikrotik-router
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-06-26T15:38:29.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Authentication

Chris_Hanson

(Employee) asked a question.

June 23, 2023 at 2:46 PM

Configuring an IPSec Tunnel in RouterOS (Mikrotik Router)

In this walkthrough, my goal is to route a subnet (192.168.2.0/24) through an IPSec tunnel to Zscaler’s Atlanta II node.

Within the ZIA Portal

Define Your Location

Navigate to Administration -> VPN Credentials

Keep FQDN checked

Provide a User ID and domain

Create a Pre-Shared Key (you will need this again later). I used

this site

to create a randomized 30-character alphanumeric key.

Navigate to Administration -> Location Management

Make sure you associate the newly created VPN Credentials with this location.

Within RouterOS

Establish IPSec Tunnel Connectivity

Log in to your Mikrotik router console. The default address is 192.168.88.1. You can run the following commands (click Terminal in the top right) to build the required configuration or use the GUI.

Turn on Safe Mode!

If you make a configuration error that causes you to lose the ability to connect to your router, that change will be reverted automatically while in safe mode. The alternative is having to physically reset your router to factory settings.

Create the IPSec Profile. You can paste this exactly into the terminal.

/ip ipsec profile add dh-group=modp1024 dpd-interval=30s

name

="Zscaler Profile"

Create the Zscaler IPSec Peer. Use

this site

to find the node you want to peer with. Make sure to copy the VPN Host Name and not the Proxy Host Name! This example uses Zscaler Atlanta II.

/ip ipsec peer add address=

atl2-vpn.zscalertwo.net

exchange-mode=ike2 name="ZScaler Atlanta II" profile="Zscaler Profile"

Create the IPSec Proposal. You can paste this exactly into the terminal.

/ip ipsec proposal add enc-algorithms=aes-256-cbc,aes-192-cbc,aes-128-cbc,null name="Zscaler Proposal"

Create the IPSec Identity. You must replace the highlighted fields with the configured VPN credentials from the ZIA portal. This example uses the peer I created for Zscaler Atlanta II.

/ip ipsec identity add my-id=user-fqdn:[YOURUSER@YOURDOMAIN.COM]

peer

="ZScaler Atlanta II" secret=[YOUR_ALPHANUMERIC_PRE-SHARED_SECRET]

Create the IPSec Policy. In this example, I am only routing subnet 192.168.2.0/24 through the IPSec tunnel.

/ip ipsec policy add dst-address=0.0.0.0/0 peer="ZScaler Atlanta II" proposal="Zscaler Proposal" src-address=192.168.2.0/24 tunnel=yes

Create a Firewall NAT rule that accepts IPSec packets. In my example, I want subnet 192.168.2.0/24 to be routed through the IPSec tunnel.

/ip firewall nat add action=accept

chain

=srcnat ipsec-policy=out,ipsec src-address=192.168.2.0/24

If your IPSec tunnel has successfully connected to Zscaler, you should see the following…

…within RouterOS (IP -> IPSec)

…and within the ZIA Portal (Analytics -> Tunnel Insights -> Logs)

ZIA - Authentication

Should you activate Fallback to GW Domain and activate Failover to the 2nd DC in PAC ?

Hello Zscaler Community,

I have a Question about this Feature "Fallback to Gateway Domain"

Should you activate this function in general or do you have to set something else somewhere ?

Fallback to Gateway Domain: Select this checkbox when PAC proxies cannot be reached for Zscaler Tunnel (Z-Tunnel) 1.0, Zscaler Client Connector falls back to the gateway domain.

The other Question is what should be the correct order

We use Custom PAC File and there is a directly accessible list. And also some ByPass Lists for Microsoft Services.

In first section is directly accessible list and after this is the "Default Traffic Forwarding."

/* Default Traffic Forwarding. Forwarding to Zen on port 80, but you can use port 9400 also */

return "PROXY ${COUNTRY_GATEWAY}:80; PROXY ${COUNTRY_SECONDARY_GATEWAY}:80; DIRECT";

After this comes ByPass List with Microsoft Services

And then in the End "Manual Failover to the Secondary DC"

/* Manual Failover to Secondary Data Center, However, if the primary data center is unavailable for any other reason, such as ISP issues, latency issues, Microsoft issues etc.*/

return "PROXY ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY_FX}:80; PROXY ${GATEWAY_FX}:80; DIRECT";

Is this influenced by this or does it have nothing to do with each other?

akita_down

I had a similar request from a customer as well and I see the value but at the same time what is the security risk?

ZIA is mainly used to access internet applications, primarily to block threats rather than allowing access to sensitive information.

Unless the customer uses strict enforcement and is blocking all outgoing traffic until ZIA is authenticated, someone can access e-mail regardless of Zscaler authenticating or not.

This article gives some info on the cookie authentication methods of ZIA -

About User Authentication Frequency | Zscaler

If you do happen to find something to force reauthentication - I'd be interested to hear about it.

Is there a way to use File Type Control based on the user agent ?

Hello,

I know it's possible to define URL filtering rules based on user agents, but I can't find a way to do the same with file type control. This would allow standard users to download their software updates while preventing them from downloading msi and other dodgy software from their browsers. Do you know if there's anything in the roadmap about this?

Thanks !

ZIA - URL Filtering

4 answers

511 views

manuel

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hey adreynaud,

interesting idea but for me (!) it sounds like "security through obscurity" as every user can modify user-agent without any local admin permissions quite easily. Therefore relying on useragent IDs will not help here I fear ;-). I would recommend to restrict local admin access and enable particular Zscaler services like sandboxing and URL categories to catch the worst.

To lock things further down you can make use of applocker rules with dedicated allow and deny rules, monitoring via Defender and Sentinel-Integration... But this is a another story :-D

BR

Manuel

adrienr

(Customer)

3 years ago

Thanks for your reply.

The idea is to only prevent standard endusers from downloading stuff from untrusted sources. The absence of restrictions gives the false impression that anything not explicitly blocked is permitted.

There are always ways around the restrictions for more advanced users. But unlike standard users, they're less likely to unwittingly download junk from untrustworthy sources. Moreover, anyone who is perfectly aware that there are restrictions, but who intentionally seeks to circumvent them, also knows that they are exposing themselves to serious consequences.

As for Applocker, I've been through a "successful" deployment, but it's been absolute hell.

upgradeyard

(Customer)

3 years ago

As of my last knowledge update in September 2021, I am not aware of any native or built-in feature in web browsers that allows file type control based on user agents. Web browsers typically do not offer this level of granular control for file downloads based on user agents.

File type control or content filtering is usually done on the server-side or through network devices like firewalls or web proxies. In these cases, you can configure rules to filter and block specific file types based on various criteria, including user agents. However, this kind of control is not typically implemented directly within web browsers.

If you are looking to implement file type control based on user agents for a specific use case, you may need to explore server-side solutions or network-level content filtering options. These solutions can provide more comprehensive control over the types of files that users are allowed to download, based on the user agent or other criteria.

As for the roadmap of specific web browsers or content management systems, it's challenging to provide up-to-date information beyond my last update in September 2021. Browser features and capabilities may have evolved since then, so I recommend checking the latest documentation and release notes of the web browsers you are interested in to see if any new functionalities related to file type control have been introduced.

Additionally, if you are using a specific content management system or firewall solution, it's best to refer to their official documentation or contact their support team to inquire about the availability of file type control based on user agents in their products.

For more information check this:

yardgearsguide.com

## GRE tunnels on a Checkpoint Firewall cluster

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009mU4SXCA0/gre-tunnels-on-a-checkpoint-firewall-cluster
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-02-06T12:49:55.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Raj90909

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited July 13, 2023 at 6:05 PM

GRE tunnels on a Checkpoint Firewall cluster

Has anyone been able to setup GRE tunnels on a Checkpoint cluster, consisting of 2 firewall members in an active/standby configuration? The firewall cluster has 2 members with only a single member active at any time and passing traffic. There is an external interface VIP which is configured for egress traffic.

We have GRE tunnels setup on standalone firewalls, which Checkpoint has a solution for in

sk175385

. This is working just fine. However, a cluster configuration seems to be the issue.

When provisioning a new GRE tunnel from the ZIA portal, you are provided with a /29 internal GRE IP range for 2 tunnels, consisting of 4 usable IPs (2 for local and 2 for peer), for a single static IP that is provided.

We were informed that the same configuration must be applied to both members. However, in doing so, we cannot as firewall members part of a cluster cannot have duplicate interface IPs. We essentially require 4 tunnels for a single IP that is provisioned. Checkpoint has a document published into their community, which mentions creating 2 separate tunnel configurations (ie: two /29 subnets). Trying to see if Zscaler is able to allocate a /28 internal GRE IP range instead for 4 tunnels.

Looking for guidance.

ZIA - Forwarding

3 answers

1.82K views

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

I've not set this up before but wouldn't you use the VRRP address to build the GRE tunnels from.

KamZet

(Customer)

2 years ago

Check Point Cluster

Zscaler only offers a /30 subnet mask for their GRE tunnel for the internal tunnel addresses.

In a /30 network, only two of the four IPs can be used for hosts. The first and last IP of the subnet are used for the network ID and the broadcast address respectively.

In a Check Point cluster with two members you normally already need three IPs. So what can be done? There is the possibility to configure the member IPs to another subnet than the VIP.

You need one "scopelocal" route per GRE interface on each cluster. This looks then with two GRE tunnels like this:

set static-route

192.168.100.0/30

nexthop gateway logical gre1 on

set static-route

192.168.100.0/30

scopelocal on

set static-route

192.168.200.0/30

nexthop gateway logical gre2 on

set static-route

192.168.200.0/30

scopelocal on

sainathg

(Partner)

a year ago

Hello ,

As i was failed in establishing ipsec tried the below for GRE

On the checkpoint Giai , use different subnet for ipv4 address  ( ex. 192.168.168.1 )and peer address should be the zscaler end ip ( ex. 172.22.x.3 /30 ) , subnet 30 , ttl 225  on GRE interface window . Similarly do the config on secondary cluster member using 192.168.168.2 and peer address should be the zscaler end ip ( ex. 172.22.x.3 /30 ) . After that on smart console go to network managemnt and click on the interface with topology tab both the members Gre interface will be visible then add the virtual ip add for the gre interface ( 172.22.x.2/30 ) and also create a policy from 192.168.168.1-2  to 172.22.x.x/30 . install the policy and try to ping the peer ip 172.22.x.3 from both the members .

also a polci should be there from any to zscaler public edge ips with services ping and GRe. u can verify the logs with the filter of 192.168.168.1 or 2 as source , the source 192.168.168.1 or 2 will be nated as 172.22.x.1  and the destination would be 172.22.x.3

Regards

<!-- ZS-POST {"url":"https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009nNSa5CAG/can-zscaler-ocr-blocks-be-distinguished-from-edm-blocks","lastmod":"2023-08-01T05:43:56.000Z","id":"0D54u00009nNSa5CAG"} -->
## Can Zscaler OCR blocks be distinguished from EDM blocks?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009nNSa5CAG/can-zscaler-ocr-blocks-be-distinguished-from-edm-blocks
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-08-01T05:43:56.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Policy Rules

jennifer.weber

(Customer) asked a question.

July 20, 2023 at 5:15 PM

Can Zscaler OCR blocks be distinguished from EDM blocks?

We have a need to know how many DLP incidents were a result of an OCR block. With this in mind, is there a way to determine or count the number of OCR blocks? I don't think there is as my understanding is that Zscaler OCR is used in tandem with EDM in a DLP Rule. Therefore, I assume we'd just see an EDM block, but it wouldn't specifically say whether that was the result of an OCR block. However, I could be mistaken and missing something here with whether Zscaler can show us how many of the EDM blocks were the result of an OCR block?

Policy Rules

1 answer

370 views

rkhalid

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hey Jennifer.

You can place a rule without OCR above a duplicate rule that has OCR enabled, thats the short and easy answer.

Other thoughts:  Currently the best way to check all the fields and values that we are capturing is within our Incident Management tool with automated workflows that will display the metadata for violations as well as give you the ability to pull down the violating file.  You can also see fields and values in a tabular view in the logs.  Furthermore, an email can also be sent to an auditor with the above mentioned metadata and violating file.  In all of these sources there are some fields that may be of interest, however, there is currently not a distinguisher that states OCR is the process within this rule that caught this.  Some fields that may be of interest are upload file name and upload file type which would help capture pure image uploads.  Content type and document type are also fields to keep track of.

Thanks and please let me know if you have any further questions.

Raja Khalid

Data Protection Architect

Microsoft Power Automate Desktop

The software installs a service in Windows named 'Power Automate service' (UIFlowService) that runs with a local account '

Has anyone of you achieved to get '

Simon

GordonWright

(Customer)

I'd be surprised if most of the URL's where not already allowed in your policy. Especially if you are an O365 customer.

All the connections are on HTTPS so you only need to add a rule to the URL Control policy.

You can either allow the URL Category that these domains are a member of or define a Custom Category and add all the domains to it.

I couldn't see a pre-defined Cloud App for use in the policy.

## Separated iDP for ZIA admin vs ZIA users authentication

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009sTgkuCAC/separated-idp-for-zia-admin-vs-zia-users-authentication
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-08-21T10:03:28.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Authentication

avshch

(Customer) asked a question.

August 14, 2023 at 6:20 PM

Separated iDP for ZIA admin vs ZIA users authentication

Hello,

I can see an option to add multiple iDP on ZIA side, but no option to bind ZIA admin to a specific iDP.

Is it possible to defined a separated iDP for ZIA admin from ZIA users?

For example ZIA admin authentication with Okta and ZIA users authentication with Google iDP?

Thanks,

ZIA - Authentication

3 answers

371 views

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi,

Yes you can do that. You configure SSO for admins in

Administration > Administrator Management

rather than in

Authentication Settings

like the user idp section.

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-saml-admins

Just a reminder, admin SSO does not support provisioning, so you will have to create the administrator in the ZIA admin portal first. If the admins for your admin idp have a different domain, you will need to submit a support ticket to get the new domain added to your tenant so that you can create admins with that username.

avshch

(Customer)

3 years ago

@mrockey

(Employee)

​ Do you mean to have admin usernames aliased with @

domain1.com

and regular users with @

domain2.com

This way ZIA would be able to differentiate which iDP to use for authentication?

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hey. It doesn't really matter, you can still do a different IDP for admin SSO vs user SSO even if the domains are the same. It's just that it's more common for different IDPs to have different domains.

I make a quick video (no audio) showing my setup with user SSO for

rockeylab2.com

using AzureAD and admin SSO for

rockeylab2.com

using Okta.

https://www.loom.com/share/a597be1e8be945198b0b214ff7b88725?sid=27232782-904e-4a79-87d5-33f41fffefd9

## Limit O365 to our Tenant

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009vVEAyCAO/limit-o365-to-our-tenant
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-09-06T17:23:16.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - URL Filtering

JayMan

(Customer) asked a question.

August 29, 2023 at 4:05 PM

Limit O365 to our Tenant

Hi All,

I've been trying to find the instructions but I don't seem to be able to.

I want to block all O365 access, Outlook.com Hotmail.com etc...

BUT allow our Tenant only. I have the tenant profile setup but I am not sure how to now block all the non-authorized ones.

ZIA - URL Filtering

2 answers

1.51K views

Dustin

(Customer)

3 years ago

You will need to create a cloud app policy under URL & Cloud App Contro to allow the traffic, the tenant field is under the action options. Then create another policy under it to block the same app without the tenant selected.

1 like

mrockey

(Employee)

3 years ago

Hi!

The steps to do this are:

create a tenant profile for Microsoft login services

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/adding-tenant-profiles

create a cloud app control rule in position 1 for Microsoft login services. It's under the IT services category. Make this an allow rule and select the tenant profile you created from the drop down.

Create a cloud app control rule under the above rule. Make this a block rule and select Microsoft login services.

Save and apply changes. Now your users will be able to login to only your O365 tenant, and not any other tenant.

ZIA: SCIM false Redundant Exports

Hi Zscaler Community,

Recently we migrated to Azure AD and using SCIM provisioning. Some users reported that they were getting policy blocks for URLs that are allowed by the company policy. I checked their accounts in ZIA User management and saw that the default AAD group that all employees get for enforcing the default company policy was not assigned.

Afterwards I checked that particular AAD group to see if the user was a member of it and he indeed was a member. This means that SCIM should have been synced to ZIA User management and the group should have been assignd in ZIA User Management after the sync. As I said before, user was not assigned the group in ZIA User Management.

Therefore, I provisioned the AAD group on demand for this specific user and AAD skipped the request and returned a "RedundantExport" as reason. So AAD thinks the group is already properly synced to ZIA User Management. This is not the case.

How to reproduce:

Remove AAD group from any account in ZIA User Management.

Provision that specific group for that specific user in AAD.

Please find Skip Reason below:

Workaround: add the user manually to the group in ZIA User Management.

Has anyone else experienced this or are you able to reproduce?

Thanks in advance,

Kevin.

(Customer) asked a question.

September 8, 2023 at 3:30 PM

CISCO Umbrella to ZScaler Migration approach

Working on one of the client requirement for migrating their CISCO Umbrella configuration to ZIA. Do we have any migration approach documentation to replicate the URL/SSL configuration to ZIA instead of manual replication of each policies?

ZIA - URL Filtering

2 answers

968 views

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

3 years ago

If the customer has the Advanced Cloud Firewall add on, you can easily build the "DNS" policies on a like for like.  You can then point the customer's internal DNS servers to Zscaler's DNS servers using known locations where Advanced Cloud Firewall is on.

For the long term approach I would evaluate each and every rule to see if it can be achieved with a Cloud App Contorl policy over a URL filtering policy.

1 like

GordonWright

(Customer)

3 years ago

I try to avoid doing a like-for-like copy because it always brings across all the bad/poorly configured stuff as well as the good/well configured stuff.

ZIA has some great API's available to make this migration easier.

## Unable to login to Facebook / Meta Business portal

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009zdp0nCAA/unable-to-login-to-facebook-meta-business-portal
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-10-21T07:37:15.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - URL Filtering

returnZero

(Customer) asked a question.

September 20, 2023 at 3:09 AM

Unable to login to Facebook / Meta Business portal

A number of our users utilize Facebook / meta business portal to run social media ad campaigns.

Recently, they've all had issues logging into business.facebook.com. After entering the username/password and MFA token (either SMS or google auth) they just get an error for Facebook and forced to log out and log back in again - going in a continuous loop.

Note:

Disabling Zscaler client app fixes issue.

Turning it back on, causes issue to immediately return.

Running with tunnel v1

Appears to affect accounts with Facebook MFA enabled, both SMS and/or Google Authenticator

Things tried:

Adding the domains to whitelist from SSL inspection has not helped.

## Handling DNS request type "ANY" with ZIA Cloud Firewall and DNS Control

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009zgqNaCAI/handling-dns-request-type-any-with-zia-cloud-firewall-and-dns-control
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-09-25T15:52:33.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Stefan Sebastian

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited September 25, 2023 at 3:52 PM

Handling DNS request type "ANY" with ZIA Cloud Firewall and DNS Control

What is DNS request type "ANY"?

The DNS request type "ANY" is an auditing, information, or reconnaissance method of asking a DNS server to return all records for the specified domain. For example, if you make an ANY request for

example.com

it will return all A, MX, SOA, NS, SPF, TXT and other entries the DNS server has specifically for

example.com

Sometimes a list of records is quite long and exceeds the 512B standard UDP packet size. In cases like these, the DNS server will return as much as what fits into the UDP-based response and indicate that the record is truncated through the TC flag. This usually prompts the client side to re-send an ANY request via TCP so the entire list of records can be returned.

Legitimate and malicious uses of ANY requests

DNS servers responding to recursive queries have a necessarily limited view of all possible DNS resolutions globally. When queried, a DNS server will seek to resolve any given query by asking another DNS server (and so on) or iterating through the hierarchy of authoritative DNS entries starting from one of the core 13 root resolvers to a top level domain authority for ".com" or ".de" and eventually to the authoritative DNS for "example.com". That authoritative DNS will provide the latest official answer for request like A-record queries that tell the requestor that "example.com" can be found at IP address "1.2.3.4" -- and other information like "there is also an address for sending mail to example.com" (an MX record) etc.

ANY requests are used to find all the possible record types and their values for a domain in a single request so a user doesn't have to request all possible record types sequentially. This is done legitimately to audit existing records and to quickly assemble or share info.

Unfortunately, the fact that a single request can result in a disproportionately large response and considering that DNS request sources can be forged, together mean that ANY requests are a way to launch reflective DNS attacks. Also, in simply in generating the response, the DNS server consumes more DNS server resources than regular, one-time queries. Finally, ANY is used by attackers to build a picture of the attack surface of any given organization including multi-tenant ones.

Recursive cache resolvers and Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR)

Because of the niche application of ANY requests and their comparative threat, most DNS services have deprecated the support of ANY requests. This is particularly if true the DNS service are cacheing servers for recursive queries. This is less true of authoritative DNS like those provided by domain registrars who must propagate their clients' DNS entries.

The Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR) responds to recursive requests from users or DNS forwarders. On the backend, it makes iterative queries and uses DNSSEC when authoritative DNS servers it interacts with supports it. ZTR then caches the values it has been asked for the TTL of the entry so it doesn't need to spend time and resources doing further iterative lookups every time it is asked and the record is remains valid.

ZTR is not an authoritative DNS provider but queries various authoritative DNS servers to resolve the queries it gets asked. Like any DNS public recursive resolver, ZTR will never have the full list of all possible records for a given domain. So when ZTR receives an ANY request, at most it will respond with what is in the cache. So if ZTR does have a response for ANY that is not a SERVFAIL (null) then it will be any resolutions that have been previously provided that haven't exceeded their TTL.

Deprecation of DNS ANY requests and End of Support

DNS ANY requests are decreasingly supported by DNS resolvers on the internet. This is due to of the above noted security threats, the sensibility of supporting the operation on caching DNS servers, and the added processing required to support a capability of questionable value at best.

Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR) is targeting a complete End of Support for DNS request type "ANY". Some data centers will no longer support ANY requests at all while others may continue until such time that End of Support is complete.

Best practices for ANY type requests

Due to the deprecation and impending End of Support for ANY type requests on the internet, it is therefore imperative to either no longer send ANY type requests generally (recommended) or bypass the few users who may continue to have a legitimate use for ANY requests from resolving at ZTR. This transits the DNS traffic but the requests still get DNS Control policy applied to them.

A key caveat is that ZTR is a safe and highly available DNS resolver that is accessible in all Zscaler data centers and very few users should be granted a bypass from ZTR resolutions if that rule is in fact enabled in Cloud Firewall policy (in the console: Policy -> Firewall Control, NAT Control Policy tab).

In NAT Control Policy, create a new rule ranked higher than the system-defined "Zscaler Trusted DNS Resolver". The new, higher ranked rule will take precedence over the ZTR rule which directs all DNS requests to the ZTR (and is directed to ZTR regardless of where the user originally wanted to use as a DNS resolver).

The new NAT rule needs have the Network Service "DNS" selected as a condition (meaning it will apply to any dest TCP/UDP:53 traffic) and all users or groups or other subset/division of users that will be granted an exception to use ANY type requests.

The action is destination NAT to port 53. Do not enter an IP address in the action unless you want all DNS queries to go to that location. Using only the port number, the rule essentially says "whatever IP address he user originally wanted but it must be sent via dest:53". One of the two values must be present to complete the action in any case.

Save and activate the rule.

This will now transit all DNS for the selected subset of users. All other users will get the subsequent rule (redirect to ZTR for example). All DNS Control security inspections continue to still be applied to this DNS traffic.

Remote users with Client Connector and tunnel 2

For any users using Client Connector -- either remote or at a Location -- tunnel 2 needs to be enabled. Tunnel 2 potentially captures all non-web including DNS traffic and sends it via DTLS tunnel to the Zscaler Public Service Edge.

This also presents another bypass option: when a Client Connector user needs to make DNS ANY requests

and

the permissions allow then temporarily disabling Client Connector, this would mean that the ANY requests does not come to Zscaler. But it also means no traffic comes to Zscaler while the Client Connector is disabled and is a security risk.

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

## Best practice for CFW rules with network application (DPI) detections as condition

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A0dGk2CQE/best-practice-for-cfw-rules-with-network-application-dpi-detections-as-condition
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-11-30T20:24:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Stefan Sebastian

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited November 30, 2023 at 8:24 PM

Best practice for CFW rules with network application (DPI) detections as condition

Network Apps detections in CFW rules

The use of deep packet inspection (DPI) in firewall rules was once considered revolutionary more than 15 years ago with the creation of a new type of firewall called "next generation firewalls" or NGFWs. DPI independently identifies applications by looking at a variety of behavioral and statistical aspects of communication and blends this with header and other protocol communication values. This is done to get certainty the application generating the flow and for a corporate decision on whether that application should be allowed or not in certain conditions.

The nature of independently identifying traffic on the wire without assistance of the endpoints in communication means that some packets of the DPI-investigated flow need to pass on the wire before application identification certainty is achieved. Sometimes the app once identified is allowed and sometimes that app is not allowed. In either cases, these packets "leak" until the identification is complete one way or another.

Zscaler Cloud Firewall calls the DPI application identification condition in firewall rules "network applications" and anytime network applications are invoked as a rule condition, the above process happens. All firewalls behave this way when DPI is used.

Best practice in using Network Apps (DPI) in Zscaler Cloud Firewall (CFW) rules

Network applications usage in CFW should try to follow one or both of the following principles:

Network applications should always try to be joined with at least one other CFW rule condition. This can be user/group/department or network service (port and protocol), or source/dest IP address etc

Rules with network applications should be ranked as low as possible and as close as possible to to default last rule (typically a "block all" catch all rule). This allows first packet identification rules to match and execute sooner and the network app rule to take longer while impacted as few subsequent (lower ranked) rules as possible

Example leading to best practice recommendation

Take the following example of a non-optimal ranked CFW ruleset:

Allow network app == SSH

Block network service == Telnet

Allow network service == HTTP, HTTPS, DNS

Block all (default rule setting)

Since the "Allow network app == SSH" is ranked first without additional criteria then CFW will examine every flow to identify SSH. The application identification may take several packets to identify SSH on potentially many, many flows until a determination that the traffic is or is not that network application. The CFW will keep open these flows until 1 of 2 things happen:

A). DPI terminates and either identifies or does not fully identify or

B). The inspected flow suddenly stops before DPI terminates

This ruleset is not optimally constructed since rule 2 and 3 are first packet identifications and could be excluded from DPI examination -- the CFW could have taken an immediate decision on this port/protocol traffic.

Additionally, rule 1 is too expansive for its high ranking since so much traffic (all traffic in this example) can potentially match. Another condition should be added to narrow the scope of traffic identification and/or the rule should be lowered to allow the immediate condition matching rules to match and take their actions.

Example of Optimally ranked CFW ruleset

Here is the same ruleset as above but optimally ranked:

Block network service == Telnet

Allow network service == HTTP, HTTPS, DNS

Allow network app == SSH

Block all (default rule setting)

In the above example, the "Block network service == Telnet" and "Allow network service == HTTP, HTTPS, DNS" rules are ranked higher. Since these do not use network app conditions, these rules always match on the first packet. This means that all matching flows can be immediately assessed without delay and action taken. Only the remaining subset of flows that do not match rule 1 and 2 enter the traffic identification process.

Here is the same optimally ranked ruleset but now also optimally conditioned:

Block network service == Telnet

Allow network service == HTTP, HTTPS, DNS

Allow network app == SSH AND network service == SSH

Block all (default rule setting)

In this example, the network app condition was paired with the logical AND condition by adding the network service condition to the rule. Here, the firewall only applies DPI traffic identification to flows the are TCP on destination port 22 (the definition of this particular network service). The second condition could have been a user, group, department, source IP, destination IP -- really any other condition narrows the scope of the DPI inspection so this sometimes non-first packet identification is exposed on a limited amount of flows.

This topic is related to a logging condition

When "allow due to insufficient app data" log entry value appears and when it does not.
