## Shared Devices

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A3unQ6CQI/shared-devices
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-11-04T10:17:08.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Authentication

User15799659450382128896

(Customer) asked a question.

October 11, 2023 at 8:01 PM

Shared Devices

We have a number of IOS devices that aren't attached to an individual user. They are shared devices that serve a patricular use case. We currently use pac files to forward traffic for these but we would benifit from the granularity and ability to apply the pac file using the client connector. What do people do with shared use devices that aren't authenticated with a particular user?

ZIA - Authentication

2 answers

1.15K views

postalspin

(Customer)

3 years ago

This is a tricky one, as many of these sorts of platforms assume a device is signed in by a user.   Do you have to use a PAC file or would you be open routing the traffic down a ipsec/gre tunnel to Zscaler transparently?

If you forward transaprently and make sure these devices are always on a particular subnet you could use the sublocation feature to build dedicated policies for those devices without the need for PAC files. (or if you have multiple breakouts,  use a dynamic location group to group the sublocations, and apply policies based on dynmaic location group)

If you really must have PAC files and want the ZCC to apply it then you may need to create a generic/shared user per device,  sign the generic/shared users in to ZCC and apply policies to the users (or groups if you have a lot of them).

D4rkie

(Customer)

3 years ago

We solve this by having service or functional accounts/users in AAD and use them on such shared or kiosk devices. Keep in mind that there is a technical max device per user count which is if i remember correct (15 devices per user) enforced by the platform (license limit is 5).

with ZCC and ZT20 you barely need pacfile at all since ZCC is taking all the traffic forwarding and authentication burden away from the applications and the device itself.. For sure there are exceptions cases which still require pac files but overall the pac file complexity dramtically decreases based on our experience.

Greetings

Philip

## Managing ZIA via API

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A6V4I6CQK/managing-zia-via-api
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-11-04T10:19:40.000Z

ZIA - URL Filtering

ppcc

(Partner) asked a question.

October 27, 2023 at 6:52 AM

Managing ZIA via API

Hi all, has anyone successfully used the API to configure proxy policies? While there are tools like zscaler-terraformer available, they serve different purposes.

For instance, how can we configure a rule using the API for the following scenario:

Source IP: 10.20.30.40

Destination:

example.com

Action: Allow

ZIA - URL Filtering

2 answers

537 views

Top Rated Answers

D4rkie

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hello ppcc,

if you want to deploy new configuration from scratch i would highly recommend using terraform instead of plain API.

It saves a lot of time since the main benefit is that you simply define your desired configuration and terraform ensure that it is there (deploy what is missing & delete what shouldn´t be there).

For sure it depends on your use case:

Workflow driven — API

Configuration file based we use terraform

If you simply want to give plain API a try i recommend Postman for starter since it is very quick to test.

See here:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-postman-rest-api-client

For the proxy config:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/url-filtering-policies#/urlFilteringRules-post

Keep in kind that you cannot configure proxy policies using „IP“ but locations, users, groups and device(names).

Hope that helps

Philip

## Using ZIA cookie-based user authentication with Cloud Connector

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A7AC9cCQG/using-zia-cookiebased-user-authentication-with-cloud-connector
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-12-05T17:39:29.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

Cloud Connector

dperkins

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited December 5, 2023 at 5:39 PM

Using ZIA cookie-based user authentication with Cloud Connector

Howdy Folks. Here is a guide for forcing user authentication for browser traffic using the ZIA cookie-based authentication mechanism and the Cloud Connector location/sub-location configuration parameters.

Configuration

In the endpoint:

Install the Zscaler root certificate into the VM / virtual desktop

Windows

Double-click: Install for System or Current User in the Trusted Root certificates folder

Linux (Fedora, Amazon WorkSpaces):

openssl x509 -in ZscalerRootCertificate-2048-SHA256.crt -out zscaler-root.pem -outform PEM

sudo mv zscaler-root.pem /etc/pki/ca-trust/source/anchors/

sudo update-ca-trust

Install the Zscaler root certificate into any browser that uses its own keystore

Firefox:

Navigate to Settings and then Privacy and Security. Select View Certificates. Choose Authorities, then Import, and finally select the Zscaler certificate. Choose “Trust this certificate to identify websites.”

Navigate to Settings and then Privacy and Security. Uncheck “Query OCSP responder…” under the Certificates section. NOTE: This reference architecture requires that SSL inspection be enabled for all traffic from this Location. Therefore, all traffic will be subjected to an OCSP check and the check that Firefox does is redundant.

(Optional) Enable Firefox to use the OS keystore: Navigate to “about:config”, search for and set “security.enterprise_roots.enabled” to True.

In the Cloud Connector portal:

Enable Authentication for the Cloud Connector location or a sub-location

In the ZIA portal:

(Optional) Create two URL filter policies

Enable ZIA > Administration > Advanced Settings > Enable Policy For Unauthenticated Traffic

Rule #1: Allow Auth Bypass URLs

Action: Allow

Users: Authentication Bypass URL

Rule #2: Block Unauthenticated VDI

Action: Block

Departments: Unauthenticated Transactions

Location: (CC location)

Enable SSL inspection for all traffic from the CC location

Action: Inspect

Location: (CC location)

(Optional) Block Undecryptable Traffic: True

Verification

On a virtual desktop that connects to the Internet via the configured CC location, open a web browser and navigate to any URL. We expect the browser captive portal to be shown and request the user to login to ZIA. Once this is done, checking the site connection details will show a cookie for the customer’s Zscaler cloud.

Important Notes

Note, if the SSL inspection rule is not configured then the browser captive portal will not be shown when navigating via HTTPS. Navigating to an HTTP site such as http://www.neverssl.com will initiate the captive portal. With that said, without the SSL inspection rule, even if the user logs into the captive portal via an HTTP site, subsequent HTTPS page loads will fail because the browser will not include the ZIA cookies in the request (and ZIA cannot inspect the traffic).

Helpful Links

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-zscaler-cookies

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-provisioning-authenticating-users

Cloud Connector

The on premise VZEN is used as a Source IP of our company, rather than using shared cloud nodes.  The trick is someone constructed this special list of domains at some point,  which is not supported by Microsoft, and no one wants to touch it or commit to managing it.

However, we are now being asked to bypass Zscaler completely for Microsoft authenitcation traffic so that Azure/Entra  Conditional Access can use the Source IP as a fallback mechanism to Identify devices/users (or the only ID method if the device doesn't have the full agent, which Win10 and Win 11 does, but printers etc do not.)

The catch is Microsoft do not publish, or commit to what their auth URLs are, so tightening it 100% is tricky and involves manual labour determining the URLs (and accepting risk this can change), or going a bit further and bypassing the M365 common auth links which includes more than just the auth urls.

My place have opted for the latter,  where they will eventually move to bypass Microsoft common apps from Zscaler all together.

If you are still set on trying to tighten it more, i would start at restricting the communications to line 56 under the common apps here:

Office URLs

(section starting *.

auth.microsoft.com

, *.

msftidentity.com

, *.

msidentity.com

, etc).  These look like authentication based URLs to me.

Thankfully our SD-WAN devices already define applications from the Microsoft API for common applications,  so we won't have to manually manage the rules once they are in, they should update.  Domain/FQDN firewall rules would be better as well.

Check your MTU size is optimised.

Make sure you are using the fastest not closest Service Edge. The dynamic latency-based service edge assignment in ZCC v4.x can help with this.

Dynamic Latency-based ZIA Service Edge Assignment | Zscaler

1 like

postalspin

(Customer)

3 years ago

+1 here if the issue is with remote users.  The MTU size default didnt work in our environment on DTLS 2.0 tunnels, so we had to drop it.  Also, for remote users make sure you bypass the MS Teams traffic using their inbuilt config.  That helped a lot with our teams config for remote users.

It is also important to set expectations for the end user.  if that end user has a 1Gbps intertnet line at home, they are not going to get that in my experience. but should comfortably be able to get around 100Mbps, which is fine for users.

Hello Postalpin,

Resizing the MTU didn't seem to work for us.

We have users far from the city with 20-50Mbps for their internet. Same as some office that are further too.

When using Zscaler, they go from 100Mbps to 3Mbps. It's really low to work with.

postalspin

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi Hakim,

Have you tried connecting to another Zscaler DC other than Montreal?  I know its a pain but it is worth trying if it is causing such a headache.  If there is packet loss or peering issues between some ISPs and Zscaler (saw in your post above), it is going to be a nightmare to solve as the typical "It isn't us" starts to get thrown around.  Just FYI our MTU is set to 1370 and this seems to work globally for us (Europe, Asia and the U.S)

I usually find that if users have bandwidth of 20-50 Mbps, they will usually have enough bandwidth available and the speedtest on Zscaler tests are usually a little bit lower (as an approx starting point for under 100Mbps I say Zscaler) may lose 20-30%).  agree if it drops to 3Mbps its unusable and not fit for purpose.  Also ask Zscaler support if the DC is overloaded and try an alternative one.

On the other end of the spectrum if a user has 100Mbps via Zscaler, but their ISP has 500Mbps or 1Gbps, in my opinion this isn't an issue.  A user should easily be able to use Sharepoint, onedrive etc over 100Mbps.  Bypass MS Teams so that doesnt go by Zscaler anyway as that is usually what is reccomended.  My personal experience in the UK is get 70Mbps up and down and I have no issues day to day)

If you look here:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/sd-wan-integrations-using-api

you can figure out what the Zscaler DC selections are for a public IP address and try and redirect a few users to the alt DC (or try a totally different one)

On a side note, I have constantly asked Zscaler to add a "Datacenter selection" feature in the ZCC,  so a user could switch DCs manually if they had issues,  so try and bump this up as well :)

## Hostfile Entry not working with Zscaler

- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2023-12-06T20:01:53.000Z

ZIA - Forwarding

AbhilashMohan

(Customer) asked a question.

November 27, 2023 at 4:23 PM

Hostfile Entry not working with Zscaler

I have a problem with host file entries.

We have a testing url in internet which we need to test with creating host file entries in local machine.

This works fine when Zscaler client connector is turned on ( From Home or untrusted networks).

In office, we use a GRE tunnel to Zscaler via our load balancer.

When we try to access the url from office, we see that Zscaler is overriding the host file entries and we are not able to access the testing url. Zscaler is trying to resolve the IP of url than looking at the host file.

Any idea how to fix this

ZIA - Forwarding

6 answers

2.05K views

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

3 years ago

Is your GRE tunnel forwarding all ports and protocols?  If so DNS control might be taking over the request.

AbhilashMohan

(Customer)

3 years ago

Yes , GRE tunnel forwards all protocols.

Any option to override it for a specific url. The Traffic should go via zscaler but DNS should resolve from host file

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

3 years ago

I can't think of a way to make the host file work, but I will continue to think on it.  However, you could create a DNS policy entry that might do the same thing as your hosts file.  Policy, DNS Control, Build a custom rule with a custom URL category for what you are trying to do, and then say "Network Traffic: Redirect Response" and send it to an IP that you specify.

1 like

AbhilashMohan

(Customer)

3 years ago

Thanks, But the problem here is,  its our end users who need to do host file entries often as part of their testing. So modifying DNS control does not help much

CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

You can always do this which would also work - as using the 'nix  etc host and window's host files can be problematic I do understand the need to test new URLs or Web Apps with out an invasive proxy style control in the way ----

You have ZCC installed on the systems and when your on site it would appear that your ZCC agents shut down and allow GRE to take over all forwarding. Just denying your ZCC clients for this group on site to stay enabled would not be enough as off site ZCC does not route it which leads me to believe this is going direct when off site and working properly so the GRE is the true issue with its transparent re-direction,

If you could  have your developers or web admins test under a predetermined domain ------- say

TEST.ACME.COM

----- right and whatever they are testing is just something  like this ---

qgenda.test.acme.com

On your GRE tunnel the PBR policy or ACL that dictates access just set an Object group that denies use of the GRE to destinations owned or under X ----

test.acme.com

Another option add these users devices by using DHCP reservations for IP address on site --- deny those Source IPs access to the GRE tunnel for access.

Another option have them set the by team or group or functional role (developer or Web Admin) as an example a set internally owned network range for these tests and have them leverage internal DNS to avoid the GRE tunnel for outbound traffic as internally they could be on  a 172.16 -31 or a 192.168 range and since RFC 1918 does not go to Zscaler by default it also won't go to the GRE

CKAIJA

(Employee)

3 years ago

One advantage to using PBR with Object group driven variables is you can add and modify that object group at will with out interrupting the GRE configuration or traffic it just picks up the new variable and continues trucking down the road

## Why is a tunnel needed?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ADG3fKCQT/why-is-a-tunnel-needed
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-03-13T09:56:10.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Ex-engineer

(Customer) asked a question.

Edited December 15, 2023 at 4:24 AM

Why is a tunnel needed?

<p>I understand that traffic that is going to be secured and have policies apply to It has to be routed to the Zen box or the provider service edge edge, as it is called. But

WHY

does a GRE or IPSEC tunnel have to be built? Web traffic is headed out to the internet from, say, a corporate site, so why can't the traffic leaving the site just get routed the normal way (without a tunnel) through the internet to this Zscaler Zen box? I do not understand the purpose of the tunnel. </p>

ZIA - Forwarding

4 answers

708 views

Top Rated Answers

postalspin

(Customer)

3 years ago

So the IPSEC/GRE connectivity is designed to be used at corporate locations where there is a firewall, router etc that allows corporate locations to be connected to the Zscaler Internet Access (ZIA Cloud).  Zscaler has a concept of "locations" which is a connectivity point from your perimter to ZIA .  I tend to use the terms

Parent location

(public IP) and

Sub location

(private IP) to differentiate between the 2 types clearly.

The main benefit the tunnel provides is it allows you to preserve the Internal source IP as you hit ZIA for all traffic because you can disable NAT inside the tunnel.  You can then build policies based on your RFC1918 Addresses using sub locations.  You can also use the RFC1918 addresses in Firewall rules.  If you didnt have a tunnel, you would need to identify seperate devices/subnets by public ip so you would burn through them quite quickly (theoretically).

let's imagine you have a client network, server network and guest network.  You could create sub locations for each of these and have different settings enabled.  E.G

Client Network- 10.0.0.0/24 - Auth ON, SSL INspection ON, Firewall ON, IPS ON

Server Network - 10.0.1.0/24 - Auth OFF, SSL Inspection ON, Firewall ON, IPS ON

Guest Network: 10.0.2.0/24 - Auth OFF, SSL INspection OFF, Firewall ON, IPS ON.

other (any other traffic generated form the location): Auth: ON, SSL Inspection ON, Firewall ON, IPS ON

Second, this in turn makes it a bit kinder when looking through logs as you can simply query by your source private IP,  rather than having to translate public ips to private and map the source/dest ports etc.

Finally, It also provides a bit of protection for the platform to stop just anyone using it. For ipsec you need to authenticate the tunnel. To create the GRE tunnels you need to register your source public IP and select yours DCs.

Hope that helps :)

Selected as Best

All Answers

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

3 years ago

Traffic forwarding is important because it ensures that the traffic from users/ servers/IOT/ guests needs to reach to Zscaler cloud for policy enforcement.

Sent traffic to Zscaler service edge,  (PAC, ZCC, GRE/IPSEC/ Port forwarding)

If your sources are user machine, and capable of install an agent , ZCC is the best option.

If your sources doesn't option to install ZCC agent go with PAC file with few degraded features, like one time authentication.

If your sources are servers, guest , or IOT subnets , then go with GRE / IPSEC tunnel, recommended is GRE as it is less overhead.

When your go with Port forwarding , NAT concepts will add up latency and overhead in the infrastructure.

KLee

(Customer) asked a question.

December 21, 2023 at 9:47 AM

What is the difference between Public Edge Service IP and the Virtual Proxy IP given from the ip.zscaler.com?

Hi

Trying to understand what is the different between the Public Service Edge IP (165.225.0.0/17) and the Virtual proxy IP (136.226.234.13) as well as request arriving from this IP address (136.226.234.107) ?

From-> ip.zscaler.com , extracted information as below;

Your request is arriving at this server from the IP address 136.226.234.107

The Zscaler proxy virtual IP is 136.226.234.13.

The Zscaler hostname for this proxy appears to be zsn-sin4-3e4-sme.

Thanks.

ZIA - Forwarding

2 answers

1.02K views

Top Rated Answers

G-Man8

(Customer)

3 years ago

Your request is arriving at this server from the IP address 136.226.234.107 --> is exact proxy server or SMA (as per Zscaler) which handles your traffic.

The Zscaler proxy virtual IP is 136.226.234.13 --> is Zscaler' s load balance server.

The Zscaler hostname for this proxy appears to be zsn-sin4-3e4-sme.

Connectivity flow:

Machine (private IP) ----> NAT device(Public IP)------> Zscaler Loadbalancer -----> Zscaler SMA server—>

ip.zscaler.com

First line can be interpreted as

"Your request is arriving at this server(

ip.zscaler.com

webpage) from the IP address Zscaler SMA server.

Credit to @Ganesh Krishnan

Hi Team,

Mayank

ZIA - Authentication

Armando

(Employee)

Hi @Mayank Vyas​ In this scenario, authentication will be handled through the browser and will be based on the "road warrior" location. However, if you have a dedicated port assigned per user, the location can also be mapped directly to that dedicated port.

Beyond this, the authentication setup remains the same as it would be when using either the Zscaler app or a PAC file.

G-Man8

Hi Diode,

I was going to suggest you move away from ZCC 3.6 due to high CVE.

ZCC 4.3 is Globally available now and does offer loads of enhancements.

So if you are 100% sure you'll be going with Option 3 then let's give it a go :)

Recommend creating 2x new App Profiles:

1)'Test WFP Driver' App profile (Requires ZCC 4.3) so you dont impact Production with the new 'Install WFP Driver'.

The 'Install WFP Driver' is required for the 'Process-based' bypass.

2) 'Test Enrolment' App Profile which get's assigned using your test 'Policy Token' during ZCC install.

This App Profile also requires you to enable 'Install WFP Driver' which makes 'PROCESS-BASED APPLICATION BYPASSES' visible for you custom 'Remote Control' bypass.

https://help.zscaler.com/client-connector/adding-process-based-applications-bypass-traffic

Please review the various 'Matching Criteria' and enter the path to your remote control EXE/EXE's.

Note: If you opt for 'Certificate Signer' then using PS Get-AuthenticodeSignature -FilePath "

C:\your

remote control EXE" is easier.

Once you've created your custom Remote Control Process Bypass it should be a question of installing ZCC using your 'Test Enrolment' App Profile.

As your 'Test Enrolment' App Profile (via Policy Token) is being loaded before the user Authenticates you should see the 'Update Policy' option as shown below.

Try to remote control to this device and kindly share the result.

Thank you

Regards

G-Man8

(Customer)

3 years ago

Hi Diode,

Few options here :)

I assume you are using a 'Policy Token' during your strict enforcement ZCC enrolment which provides you with some flexibility depending on your requirements:

1) Create an 'Enrolment' App Profile (using Policy Token) which applies before the user authenticates within ZCC and assign cloud PAC with your remote control bypasses (Supported by Zscaler)

2) Create an 'Enrolment' App Profile and add your "remote control" bypasses to 'VPN Bypass' if they dont use wildcards (

Not

recommended by Zscaler)

3) Create an 'Enrolment' App Profile and consider testing ZCC 4.3 using 'Process-based' Application Bypass for your remote control EXE.

Please note I haven't tested option 3 yet but it's on my list.

Kindly share your decision and test results

Thank you

fabio.goncalves

(Customer) asked a question.

January 12, 2024 at 7:52 PM

Zscaler Secure Browsing x Embedded Chromium in Different Softwares

So, I would like to reach the community here to check and get some feedback on a behavior regarding Browse Control in Secure Browsing that we've been detecting in Zscaler since its implementation in our company a year ago. Basically, we've setup the rule to block any communication from Older Versions of any type of browser, which is a best practice to protect and avoid exploration of browse vulnerabilities.

However, it is not uncommon for client-based applications to have an embedded browser in them, normally Chromium engines. Some popular examples from our user cases here are 3Ds Max Studio from Autocad and other engineering solutions. Normally the Chromium is only used to check licensing from a specific service from the software manufacturer and is used only during the session start of the application.

The catch here is: Chromium Engines are detected by Zscaler as Chrome, and generally these are forgotten to be updated by manufacturers. So, I would like to understand if:

1- Do any of you faced this issue as well?

Just to give our perspective, what we've been doing here is treating this as a case by case situation, always trying to enforce with the software manufacturer the need to patch their solution, but this is not always possible and feasible in a timely manner.

2- Is the risk of these Chromium engines being used in an attack the same as a web browser?

Since it is embedded into a software, I couldn't find evidences that this could be a valid attack vector, because it is too specific. The best I found was an article from 2020 where a company was attacked but the vulnerability was from 3ds Max Studio as a whole, not from the chromium engine specifically.

3- This one is for Zscaler Developers - Couldn't Zscaler differentiate an Embedded Chromium Engine from a Chrome Web Browser?

I don't know if it is possible, if so, point me whether this could be a nice ER to send.

ZIA - Posture

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hey Prathap,

you cannot "block" installation or usage of chrome extensions with Zscaler.

If you want to restrict traffic to the servers of the particular VPN extension provider you would need to identify all VPN endpoint IPs/hostnames and block these via Zscaler policy.  As this is a quite cumbersome job and obviously you would need to do so for all possible VPN providers I would recommend to restrict users from installing this extensions at all (e.g. via intune MDM Policy).

Also you may look into Zscaler Browser Isolation which will solve your issues quite easily (except license and setup efforts ;-)).

BR

Manuel

(Customer) asked a question.

January 17, 2024 at 9:19 AM

Has anyone experienced that the MD5 of a static file/s keeps on changing so Sandbox scanning never ends?

For a better security policy architecture, we set our default Sandboxing policy to scan first before provisioning. All goes well but from time to time we are getting reports of a file getting scanned in a loop. Upon further checking the web insights, we found that even though it is the same file downloaded from the same URL, the MD5 values in the logs are different so it always gets sent to the Sandbox. Has anyone experienced this for those with this type of policy?

ZIA - Cloud Sandbox

CKAIJA

(Employee)

2 years ago

Yes, the Site or browser maybe doing an auto check for connectivity or refreshing the connection that is causing the behavior. The other downside of this file your downloading is that it maybe dynamically created content so that each time the User requests it the file rehashes itself.

I have seen this behavior with DocuSign and Adobe cloud, you may need to take this URL and the Document file type for download and set it to Allow and Scan  which may help alleviate the behavior and improve end user experience

Forwarding Control

Can I use Forwarding Control policy to have some of the destinations to exit from specific Zscaler Data Center?

I've tried creating proxy and proxy gateways with a specific Zscaler datacenter proxy hostname and then tried creating Forwarding control policy to using proxy chaining with the Zscaler proxy gateway.

But I don't think it's working as expected, I see the log as "proxy chain gateway is down in zscaler"

Is this even possible? or is there any other way to do so?

User15799259994238679477

(Customer)

3 years ago

Is the goal is to have a predictable source IP, on egress to selected internet destinations?

If yes, then SIPA (Source IP Anchoring) is the solution. If you already use ZPA, you setup SIPA to forward the traffic to the destination via chosen ZPA App Connector(s).

The traffic will first go to ZIA for inspection, then it will be forwarded to ZPA, and out to the Internet through your chosen ZPA App Connector(s). SIPA works for road warriors and locations )eg; regardless of forwarding method).

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-source-ip-anchoring

If you don't already use ZPA, there is a Zscaler Managed alternative. Looks like practically the same thing, but Zscaler manage the App Connector.

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/understanding-zscaler-managed-dedicated-ip

You might also be able to get a similar path for traffic control with ZIA subclouds where the customer can steer too or remove certain DCs from use if they are seeing issues

SSL Traffic Inspected

While running the Security Policy Audit Report and reviewing SSL Inspection, I am seeing a lower than expected percentage in SSL Traffic Inspected. We have quite a number of domains in our "Do Not Inspect" SSL bypass rule. However, I feel it shouldn't be that low.

We have Office 365 One Click enabled along with Microsoft-Recommended One Click Office 365 Configuration, which automatically creates the SSL inspection rule without inspection. I'm told Office 365 One Click is excluded from the SSL %.

Armando

(Employee)

Hi @Raj Khatri​ we can take a closer look at the specific sessions you’re concerned about to determine whether they genuinely needed to bypass SSL inspection or if there’s another factor at play.

Within the report you’ve received, you can use the Web Insights to analyze those logs in greater detail. This will allow you to track the sessions and verify whether the SSL policy was appropriately applied or if adjustments are needed.

avshch

(Customer) asked a question.

February 7, 2024 at 1:51 AM

Allowing API calls from inside to the Internet via ZIA

How do we go about allowing API calls (from Postman or PowerShell) via ZIA from inside of our network to the internet?

Authentication is enforced for network location from where API call is initiated. Traffic forwarding to ZScaler via IPSEC.

Thanks,

ZIA - Authentication

1 answer

481 views

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Alex Shchukin​ As long as the API is properly authenticated and allowed on your firewall, it should function correctly with Zscaler. This is because the API requires a key to validate authentication. If the key aligns with what Zscaler expects, the connection will work seamlessly. However, if there’s a mismatch, you may encounter an error.

Zscaler SSL Cert Chain

Hi Team,

I found in Zscaler SSL Chain , these is a temp Intermediate CA with suffix (t)exist. Can anyone explain what is the purpose of this..

ZIA - SSL Inspection

1 answer

477 views

Armando

(Employee)

8 months ago

Hi @Pardeep Rawat​ The (t) suffix in the Zscaler Intermediate CA means the certificate is temporary. It’s used in SSL inspection to sign server certificates for secure traffic monitoring. These certificates are rotated regularly to maintain security and manage risks efficiently

Thanks.

## Cloud App Control Rule Order

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AIMgRBCQ1/cloud-app-control-rule-order
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-10-29T17:39:13.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - URL Filtering

kejordan

(Customer) asked a question.

February 8, 2024 at 4:52 PM

Cloud App Control Rule Order

Hi,

I am looking at my cloud app policy and we have many rules for supported and custom cloud apps. I see that they are also organized by Cloud app category. When I take a look at the rule order, I see they are numbered within their respective category.

I know that typically, rules are evaluated top down, but this gets confusing when the rules are numbered within the category.

So would the first rule checked actually be the first rule in the top category?

Ex. I have a social media URL and it is evaluated with the first rule in AI/ML category and continues down the list before moving to URL Filtering if one isn't found.

OR

Does the URL get categorized and only the cloud app rules in that category get checked?

Ex. I have a social media URL and Zscaler only checks rules in the Social Networking Category. If none are found, it checks the URL Filtering rules.

Just looking for a bit more clarification for Cloud App rule ordering and how that works. Unfortunately, all of the public documentation just says "

Cloud App Control rules are evaluated in ascending numerical order" and "They are organized by function into

categories

for easy reference and to facilitate defining rules for similar apps."

ZIA - URL Filtering

1 answer

588 views

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Kylie Jordan​  Cloud App control rules are evaluated in the order they are listed, from lowest to highest number, where rule order \(1\) is evaluated before rule order \(2\). You can manually set the rule order number, but if Admin Rank is enabled, a higher admin rank (e.g., \(0\) being the highest) determines the rule's position, and you cannot select a rank higher than your own

## ZIA Identity Proxy - Google Workspace RPID

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AJUilYCQT/zia-identity-proxy-google-workspace-rpid
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-11-22T01:03:14.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - DLP

akita_down

(Customer) asked a question.

February 14, 2024 at 1:41 AM

ZIA Identity Proxy - Google Workspace RPID

Does anyone know if ZIA identity proxy can be configured with Google workspace using the rpid value set? (Multiple idp)

ZIA - DLP

1 answer

410 views

Corrales9602

(Employee)

8 months ago

Hello,

Yes, ZIA Identity Proxy can be configured to work with Google Workspace, and the concept of an "RPID value set" (or more accurately, the SP Entity ID of the Relying Party) is central to how ZIA's Identity Proxy functions when it's acting as the Identity Provider for your internal applications.

Let's break down how this works:

ZIA Identity Proxy's Role:

ZIA Identity Proxy acts as a Service Provider (SP) to an upstream Identity Provider (IdP) like Google Workspace. This is where users authenticate.

Concurrently, ZIA Identity Proxy acts as an Identity Provider (IdP) to your internal applications (which are the Relying Parties, or RPs). These applications don't need to support SAML natively or can centralize their SAML configurations through Zscaler.

Google Workspace as the Upstream IdP:

You configure Google Workspace as an "External IdP" within your ZIA tenant. ZIA will be the SP for Google Workspace.

Users trying to access an internal application will be redirected to ZIA, which then redirects them to Google Workspace for authentication.

Google Workspace authenticates the user and sends a SAML assertion back to ZIA.

ZIA Identity Proxy as the IdP for your Applications (where "RPID" matters):

When an internal application (your Relying Party) sends a SAML authentication request to ZIA's Identity Proxy, it includes its own unique SP Entity ID (also sometimes called Audience URI or SP ID). This  SP Entity ID is effectively what you're referring to as the "RPID value set."

In ZIA's "Identity Proxy" configuration, you define each of your internal applications as a separate "Application." For each application, you specify:

Its unique SP Entity ID.

Its Assertion Consumer Service (ACS) URL.

Which attributes ZIA should include in the SAML assertion it sends back to

that specific application

Potentially, signing certificates and other SAML assertion details.

Handling Multiple IdPs (Upstream):

ZIA allows you to configure multiple "External IdPs" (e.g., Google Workspace for users in

domain.com

, Okta for users in

partners.com

).

When an application requests authentication from ZIA's Identity Proxy, ZIA will then determine which upstream IdP to use. This determination can be based on:

Domain matching: If the user logs in with an email

user@domain.com

,  ZIA can redirect them to the IdP configured for

domain.com

IdP Chaining: You might have a default IdP, or chain them.

Specific policies: Based on groups, location, etc.

How "RPID" (SP Entity ID) helps with Multiple RPs:

When an internal application (RP1) requests authentication, it sends its  SP Entity ID (RPID_1) to ZIA. ZIA knows this is RP1, so it constructs the assertion with the correct attributes for RP1.

When another internal application (RP2) requests authentication, it sends its SP Entity ID (RPID_2) to ZIA. ZIA knows this is RP2, and constructs the assertion with the correct attributes for RP2.

Both RP1 and RP2 might be using Google Workspace as their ultimate backend authentication source (via ZIA's Identity Proxy). The SP Entity ID allows ZIA to differentiate between the applications and provide the correct assertion.

In summary:

Yes, you can use ZIA Identity Proxy with Google Workspace as the upstream IdP.

The "RPID value set" concept aligns with the SP Entity ID that each of your internal applications (Relying Parties) sends to ZIA's Identity Proxy when requesting authentication.

ZIA's Identity Proxy uses this SP Entity ID to identify

which

internal application is requesting authentication and then generates a SAML assertion tailored to that specific application, after successfully authenticating the user via Google Workspace.

You configure each of these internal applications as separate entities within ZIA's Identity Proxy settings, each with its unique SP Entity ID

## ISP DNS TRAFFIC FLOW

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AJW1ukCQD/isp-dns-traffic-flow
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-02-19T08:54:28.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Dhananjay_Bhakte

(Partner) asked a question.

February 16, 2024 at 1:33 PM

ISP DNS TRAFFIC FLOW

Hi Team,

I have Zscaler installed on my system. I am connected to home router. I got DNS ip 192.168.1.1.

In Zscaler app profile I have 192.168.0.0/16 in a destination exclusion list. So dns resolution request traffic from my system will be excluded from Zscaler.

So dns traffic is like src 192.168.1.10(system ip) destination 192.168.1.1 port 53 . and traffic will route to Home router since home router is my DNS server.

When home router enable to resolve Dns queries, it will send to ISP dns since isp dns server.is configured in home router.

Can someone help me to understand does Zscaler control dns traffic between home router and ISP dns server ? and If Zscaler intercept dns traffic how it will route to Zscaler .?

Thanks

Dhananjay

ZIA - Forwarding

5 answers

643 views

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

2 years ago

In this scenario, and assuming you are using tunnel 2 as your forwarding method ZIA is not involved in DNS resolution.   If you were using a public dns server, example 8.8.8.8 then Zscaler would see the dns traffic and intercept it.

BTW in your example above Zscaler would see the dns over https traffic and could manipulate if you set that up.

Dhananjay_Bhakte

(Partner)

2 years ago

Hi Trace,

Thank you for your response.  Yes, I am using Zscaler tunnel 2 as a forwarding method.

I am not using public dns server.

In my scenario dns server is router IP address in the machine. I am not sure how Zscaler would see dns traffic (DOH/DNS) if it is excluded in destination exclusion.

Thanks

Dhananjay

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

2 years ago

Dns over https runs over port 443 and is not controlled by the dns entries you specify in your local dns entries.  For this reason zia can be a part of the chain.   In using Google for escample, Google could tell your browser to use the Google dns over https (doh) system.   Does that make sense?

Sander from Watchmen.io

(Partner)

2 years ago

When your router is internal DNS server in your internal network you can include these DNS queries to Zscaler  with the help of your application profile.

To add specific DNS domains to send all DNS requests to the ZIA Public Service Edge through Z-Tunnel 2.0,

complete the following steps.

You can enter specific domains (e.g.,

google.com

) or enter

to include or exclude all DNS domains.

Enter the DNS domains that Zscaler Client Connector should tunnel through ZIA in the Domain Inclusions for DNS Requests field. You can include a maximum of 65,535 characters.

Enter the DNS domains that Zscaler Client Connector should not tunnel through ZIA in the Domain Exclusions for DNS Requests field. You can exclude a maximum of 65,535 characters.

Zscaler DNS Security and Control | Zscaler

-> look at this PDF

If you go to the Mobile Admin Portal, click Administration at the top, and then "Device Posture" on the left.  You can create two different postures (1) Detect Firewall (2) detect Antivirus.  You can then go into your Policies in ZPA and apply these device postures to each of the Access Policies that you want to use them on.    Let me know if you would like assistance in implementing this.

## Block Malicious IP Adress by using Malicious Content

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AKhWnjCQF/block-malicious-ip-adress-by-using-malicious-content
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-02-21T17:57:22.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

alex.albrecht1982

(Customer) asked a question.

February 21, 2024 at 1:24 PM

Block Malicious IP Adress by using Malicious Content

Hello everyone,

I have received 3 IP addresses from our security team that I should block in Zscaler: 155.133.5.15, 155.133.5.14, 118.69.65.60. Here is the source: https://www.connectwise.com/company/trust/security-bulletins/connectwise-screenconnect-23.9.8

In the firewall control I have the predefined policy "Block malicious IPs and domains" which refers to a Criteria URL Categories "Malicious Content". Where can I manage this URL category? I would like to check whether the generated IP addresses are contained in it, or enter them there and activate the policy.

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

2 answers

2.89K views

Trace Woodbury-RidgeIT

(Partner)

2 years ago

sitereview.zscaler.com

is where you can go to see where something belongs to a URL category.  If you wan to create a new IP Range for blocking you can do a new URL category or create an IP Group for this and block it in your FW policy as well.   Let me know if this helps.

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Try this:

Create an URL-Category, name it accordingly and add your 3 IP-adresses.

Then add a Firewall Filtering Rule and chose Block for URL-Category group. Take care where (= rule number) you put this rule. In case your request hits a matching allow rule (e.g. default allow http/https) before your new block rule would have no effect (rules are evaluated in the order specified and rule evaluation stop at the first match).

To mitigate any firewall rule order issues you could (!) also add an URL Filtering Rule, which blocks HTTP/HTTPS access to the same URL-Category adresses. This step is optional and depends on your rule numbering order in step 2.

Instead of an URL-Category you can also use the Destination IPv4 Group and add these to your firewall policy. IPv4 Groups of course wont work with URL&CloudApp Policies.

BR

Manuel

## ZIA Bypass/Network Troubleshooting

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AKiBuOCQV/zia-bypassnetwork-troubleshooting
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-02-22T19:58:49.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

bekkahc20

(Customer) asked a question.

February 22, 2024 at 3:07 PM

ZIA Bypass/Network Troubleshooting

Hi,

We have been working with Zscaler support but feel like we haven't been able to make our situation better; instead, it feels like we are chasing squirrels.

We are using Tunnel 2.0 with an app profile PAC file and Forwarding PAC file. The PAC files are the same, with the exception of using 'return "Direct"' in the app PAC and 'return "Proxy ${ZAPP_TUNNEL2_BYPASS}"' in the forwarding PAC for traffic intended to bypass Zscaler.

We have also tried removing some of the URLs we want to bypass Zscaler from the app PAC and adding it to the 'Hostname or IP Address Bypass for VPN Gateway." But those sites are still showing up in the web insight logs as going through Zscaler.

In the forwarding profile, we have the 'System Proxy Settings' configured with 'Enforce' and have the forwarding PAC applied as the 'Use Automatic Configuration Script.'

Most of these configurations were suggested by Zscaler support, but as I am reading more and more articles. It seems that ZTunnel 2.0 conflicts with having a Forward PAC and the 'Enforce - System Proxy" action.

Obviously, I am missing something; if anyone has suggestions or notes, I would love to test them in our environment. We are entirely remote, so each user is on their own ISP, and we are hoping to figure out how to correctly bypass Zscaler for some domains to alleviate some networking pains.

Thanks!

ZIA - Forwarding

2 answers

2.1K views

G-Man8

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hi,

Which ZCC version are you running ?

If you > 3.8 (but ideally 4.2) and purely a Tunnel 2.0 then I'll remove the PAC on Forwarding Profile.

Example Use-case:

1. Allowing to bypass domains/FQDNS without configuring the Forwarding profile PAC. Before ZCC 3.8, we needed to bypass domains both in FWD and APP profile PAC. Removes the dependency of having a system PAC enforced by Zscaler to bypass domains.

2. Allowing non-proxy aware traffic to be bypassed using domains rather than depending on IP ranges/subnets which would need to be added to tunnel 2 exclusions.

2. Allow tunnelling proxy-aware traffic via Tunnel 1.0 and rest of the traffic would be going through via Tunnel 2.0

--

Redirect web traffic to ZCC listening proxy

- When T2 is running, this flag will enable 80/443 - web traffic to our listening proxy for ZCC (default -

127.0.0.1:9000

). It can be used for bypasses using app profile PAC without the need of FWD PAC. Basically, we are forwarding all our web traffic from Tunnel 2.0 to the listening proxy and from there, app profile PAC is being used to bypass.

-- Use Z-Tunnel 2.0 for proxied web traffic -

This flag is used for proxied web traffic. When there is any traffic hitting the ZCC listening proxy. We can choose to forward it to Tunnel 2.0.

For now, all proxied traffic is at the transport layer and it's sent to tunnel 1.0 and we can send this traffic to tunnel 2.0 using this filter.

I use this method for Win11 while deploying ZCC with  strictenforcement.

Hope this helps

bekkahc20

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hi!

Thanks so much for all the info -- we are a Mac environment on 4.1.0.152.

This echoes some of the changes I was going to try next.

I wanted to try changing the forwarding profile to be route-based instead of the packet,  running a split tunnel, and removing the PAC file from the forwarding profile, as you mentioned. So the traffic I am trying to bypass Zscaler isn't intercepted at all.

Thanks again!

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ALpBBKCQ3/endpoint-fw-av-error
- Type: Q&A

AmitKhade

(Customer) asked a question.

February 29, 2024 at 6:27 AM

Endpoint Fw av error

Multiple user getting endpoint fw error and zcc logs said that communication blocked for ip 100.64.0.6 : tcp9000 at endpoint firewall.

then we have disable the firewall & antivirus in test user machine bit still getting same error.

we have whitelisted all thing which is suggested by zscaler KB article for endpoint firewall antivirus whitelisting.

please suggest next action to resolve the issue?

ZIA - Authentication

2 answers

7.61K views

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

Hello,

I am not a support person or an expert here. I am just able to search our knowledge sources and put together what I can find. Using our search tools I was able to find some information on troubleshooting this issue. All of this is based on documentation though, not from any first hand experience I have :) Let me know if this helps, as we are working on better knowledge accessibility.

Documented Troubleshooting suggestion:

The issue you're experiencing is likely due to the Zscaler Client Connector (ZCC) processes being blocked by the endpoint firewall. Here are some steps to troubleshoot:

]1. Check the ZSA tunnel logs from the time of the issue. Look for firewall blocks indicating that traffic was blocked by the firewall and ZFHM health checks were failing.

2. Observe the traffic captures. If traffic is being blocked and continuous retransmissions for the traffic are initiated, this could indicate a block from the system firewall.

3. Check the services from ZSA tray Manager logs. If there are other services running on the 9000 port, they could cause a conflict.

4. Verify the firewall/antivirus error. Check the log at '%windir%\system32\logfiles\firewall\pfirewall.log' and ensure there are no "drop" entries for (TCP) 100.64.0.6 or (UDP) 100.64.0.8 for port 80 or 9000.

5. If the issue persists, you may need to bypass the services causing the conflict or adjust your firewall settings to allow the ZCC processes. Remember to check the ZCC log data locations for more information. On Windows devices, you can find these logs at '

C:\ProgramData\Zscaler'.

## How to Forward tunel to different country data Center

(Partner) asked a question.

February 29, 2024 at 8:28 AM

How to Forward tunel to different country data Center

When a server is down or A country doesn't have a data server the proxy goes to ZEN in the nearest country. I want to instead send the traffic to a different country in this scenario. For if a person nearest ZEN is in a different country Instead of going there I want this traffic to go to a different country's Data Center which is closed to the user in that country.

For example,

IF a country has Zscaler data center to stay within the country

{return direct}

Else connect to a particular country data center closest to the user let's say USA( West, North, East South)

How would I configure this in a PAC file?

ZIA - Forwarding

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

Here is some information that I found in our knowledge sources. Preface with I have not done this myself, I  just wanted to share what I can find on our knowledge database.

To forward traffic to a different country data center, you can adjust the Application PAC file. For example, if you want to steer certain countries to the Dubai data center, you can use the following code:

if (shExpMatch(country,"United Arab Emirates")) {

/* When the User is in United Arab Emirates: use below ZEN defined */

return "PROXY

dxb1-2.sme.zscloud.net:80;

PROXY

bom4.sme.zscloud.net:80;

DIRECT";

Make sure to replace "United Arab Emirates" with the country you want to steer traffic from, and replace "

dxb1-2.sme.zscloud.net:80;

PROXY

bom4.sme.zscloud.net:80;

DIRECT" with the data center you want to steer traffic to.

Also, ensure that the data center you want to use is included in your subcloud variables. If you're using Zscaler Client Connector with Zscaler Private Access service, the data center may not be available by default. In this case, you should reach out to your technical or sales representative to have the data center made available to you.

2.How do I dynamically Forward the traffic to the nearest ZEN of a particular country to his location? (like if a person lived in Europe, Servers in East USA would be closer to the User)

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hm, maybe I missed your point, but:

Why you want to do that? Zscaler will determine the proper country based on IP-geolocation. Maybe there are multiple DC or no DC at all for some countries. So why not just let Zscaler decide which {COUNTRY_GATEWAY} will be chosen depending on the  quickest response time? You do not need to do anything here as Zscaler decides where to route traffic. If there is no {COUNTRY_GATEWAY} in your region then Zscaler choses the next and fastest {GATEWAY} - in another country - for you.

You could build a PAC file where you can implement different handling for each country (e.g. if your user is located in France you could route the traffic always to Switzerland). But thats quite prone to errors, complex to maintain and possibly quite slow (due to PAC-file size and distances).

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Yep, here in Europe we had quite often issues with wrong languages on websites due to fact there are many countries around. But most of  that issues vanished when using {COUNTRY_GATEWAY}.

In my experience users no longer complaining about performance issues easily outweigh problems with display languages (of which some can be circumvented by browser settings).

For office users you could leverage GRE tunnels, but for ZCC users you would need some kind of proxy in target country. Right now I cannot think of any approach to chain PAC-files. And besides latency I assume everything will be quite sluggish...

And what you describe sound a little bit like the hairpin tunneling of existing VPN-solutions. Would recommend to overthink that for various reasons ;-)

How To: Tunnel-less DNS Resolution using DNS Control/ZTR (Guest WiFi Users)

In this article, we will see how one can achieve tunnel-less DNS resolution by sending DNS queries to Zscaler DNS Control/ZTR without having to create a GRE tunnel.

This tunnel-less approach can be beneficial when migrating from

Zscaler Shift (now EOL)

or a 3rd party resolver, or when using a GRE/IPsec tunnel from a customer site is not an option. However, it is important to note that the recommended practice is to use Zscaler Client Connector with Z-Tunnel 2.0 (ZCC/ZT2.0) or a GRE/IPsec tunnel to route DNS traffic to ZIA whenever possible.

Note:

This tunnel-less DNS solution is not applicable for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) traffic.

Steps to Configure DNS Control/ZTR

Configure DNS server addresses on client machine

First, find out the GRE VIP addresses for the Zscaler data center closest to your network.

For this, go to

https://config.zscaler.com/

and select your ZIA cloud. In my setup, it is zscalertwo.net:

Now, go down to the data center closest your network and note down the GRE VIP addresses. Here I have chosen the San Francisco IV data center:

Note:

You can also automate this using JSON API:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/zscaler-service-endpoints

Note:

This tunnel-less DNS solution is not applicable for IPv6 DNS traffic.

On your client machine (or internal DNS forwarder), configure these GRE VIP addresses as the DNS server addresses:

Here we have configured the DNS server addresses on a Windows client machine.

Note:

In this deployment scenario, the client machine is NOT using ZCC. If the client is using ZCC with Z-Tunnel 2.0, then you should really not have a need to do it this way.

Note:

Here we chose the GRE VIP addresses from the same data center, however, you can also choose the GRE VIP addresses from two different data centers for resiliency.

Configure your ZIA Tenant

In our ZIA tenant, we need to define the location for the public IP of our client.

First, navigate to Administration > Resources > Static IPs & GRE Tunnels. Then, click on Add Static IP:

Specify the public IP of your location as will be seen by the ZIA tenant, give a name and click Next:

Specify the region and click Next.

Review and save.

Now, navigate to Administration > Resources > Location Management:

Under Locations tab: Click on Add Location:

Create a new location as shown and under "Static IP Addresses and GRE Tunnels", choose the Static IP that you had created earlier:

Note: Additionally, enable "Enforce Firewall Control" option:

Firewall, DNS and NAT Policies

Additionally, here are the screenshots for Firewall, DNS and NAT rules for reference.

Make sure that DNS traffic is allowed as shown by the below rules.

Firewall Filtering:

Note rule no 3 that allows DNS, HTTP and HTTPS traffic:

DNS Control:

By default, you have the following rules in your ZIA tenant to allow DNS traffic.

Do not add any DNS filtering rules at this stage, instead, first verify that DNS resolution is working as expected, and then you can add DNS filtering rules later on.

NAT Control:

Note:

Make sure default DNAT rule is present and enabled as shown above. This DNAT rule is what sends the DNS traffic to ZTR.

See the following for reference:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-nat-control

Verification of basic DNS resolution:

On the client machine, initiate DNS lookups:

In a following article, we will see how you can add a DNS Control policy to block access to certain restricted sites, such as gambling:

https://community.zscaler.com/zenith/s/question/0D54u0000AM61y5CQB/how-to-configure-dns-control-policies-for-tunnelless-dns-setup-guest-wifi-users

How To: Configure DNS Control policies for tunnel-less DNS setup (Guest WiFi users)

In an earlier article, we configured DNS resolution using Zscaler Trusted Resolver (ZTR) using a tunnel-less DNS setup:

https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AM6064CQB/how-to-tunnelless-dns-resolution-using-dns-controlztr-guest-wifi-users

This tunnel-less approach can be beneficial when migrating from

Zscaler Shift (now EOL)

or a 3rd party resolver, or when using a GRE/IPsec tunnel from a customer site is not an option. However, it is important to note that the recommended practice is to use Zscaler Client Connector with Z-Tunnel 2.0 (ZCC/ZT2.0) or a GRE/IPsec tunnel to route DNS traffic to ZIA whenever possible.

This article builds upon the configuration in the previous article, so make sure to complete those steps before proceeding further.

Note:

This tunnel-less DNS approach has the following limitations:

It is not applicable for DNS over HTTPS (DoH) traffic.

It is not applicable for IPv6 DNS traffic.

In this article, we will build upon that setup and add a DNS filtering rule to block gambling sites.

First, confirm that DNS resolution for a gambling site, such as 888.com is currently working on your client machine.

As one can see, DNS resolution is working and the DNS server is the one we had configured.

Configure DNS Control policy

Now, in your ZIA tenant, go to

Policy > Firewall > DNS Control

Then, click on

Add DNS Filtering Rule

and add a new rule as shown below:

Make sure to set the rule order number to be higher than the default one that allows all DNS traffic.

Note:

Zscaler supports different types of End User Notifications (EUNs) for the DNS Control policy. These EUNs are displayed to end users when their activities trigger DNS Control rules with specific actions, such as blocking traffic or redirecting responses. See the following help articles:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/dns-end-user-notifications

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-dns-control-policy

Save the rule and click on

Activation > Activate

to activate the changes.

Now, go back to the client machine and try doing a DNS lookup for 888.com - it should be blocked:

Recommended next steps

You can implement DNS filtering based on the recommended best practices:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/best-practices-dns-control-rules

Additionally, DNS control policies for some of these best practices should now be available by default in your ZIA tenant:

Critical risk DNS categories

Critical risk DNS tunnels

High risk DNS categories

High risk DNS tunnels

Risky DNS categories

Risky DNS tunnels

You can choose to either enable all or select the ones that meet your deployment needs.

Additional References

Zscaler DNS Security and Control Reference Architecture Guide:

https://www.zscaler.com/resources/reference-architectures/zscaler-dns-security-and-control-reference-architecture.pdf

siddhartha.aggarwal

(Employee) asked a question.

How To: Differentiated DNS Control Policy for Guest Wi-Fi Users (Tunnel-less DNS Setup)

In earlier articles, we saw how you can achieve tunnel-less DNS resolution by sending DNS queries to Zscaler DNS Control/ZTR without having to create a GRE tunnel, and apply DNS Control policies to such DNS traffic:

https://community.zscaler.com/zenith/s/question/0D54u0000AM6064CQB/how-to-tunnelless-dns-resolution-using-dns-controlztr-guest-wifi-users

https://community.zscaler.com/zenith/s/question/0D54u0000AM61y5CQB/how-to-configure-dns-control-policies-for-tunnelless-dns-setup-guest-wifi-users

This is especially useful, when migrating from a DNS provider, such as Zscaler Shift (now approaching EOL) or a 3rd party DNS resolver, to Zscaler DNS Control/ZTR.

One of the common requirements of such a "tunnel-less" DNS deployment is to have differentiated DNS Control policies based on the type of user or devices, such as different polices for guests/contractors vs. authorized users vs. IOT devices.

The challenge is that since all these users would reach the ZIA cloud using a common public IP, how can we distinguish them in ZIA tenant?

This can be achieved by assigning different GRE VIP addresses as DNS server addresses to the various clients/devices, and then by matching based on this GRE VIP address (in addition to the location) while selecting the DNS Control policy to be applied.

Let us look at a scenario of applying two different DNS Control policies to two different set of users:

Guest users: Block access to gambling sites

Authorized users: Allow access to gambling sites

This is just a simple example, the actual polices can vary depending on the requirements.

Note:

Here we are assuming you have a working tunnel-less DNS setup and have already configured a location for the public IP of the users and enabled firewall control for that location in the ZIA Cloud.

See the above articles for details.

Configure DNS server addresses

DNS server addresses for guest users

For example, we can assign the following two GRE VIP addresses (from two different data centers for high-availability) to the guest users:

On the client machine, configure these GRE VIP addresses as the DNS server addresses:

DNS server addresses for authorized users

Similarly, we can assign the following GRE VIP address to authorized users:

On the client machine, configure these GRE VIP addresses as the DNS server addresses:

DNS Control Policies

Note:

Here we are assuming you have already configured a location for the public IP of the users and enabled firewall control for that location.

Under Policy > Firewall > DNS Control:

For guest users:

For Guest users, we will configure a DNS Control policy to block access to gambling sites and instead send a Redirect Response.

Configure matching based on Location and specify the action as Redirect Response:

Configure matching based on GRE VIP addresses:

Match for Gambling and save the rule:

For authorized users:

For authorized users we will configure a DNS Control policy to allow access to gambling sites:

Configure matching based on Location and specify the action as Allow:

Configure matching based on GRE VIP addresses:

Match for Gambling and save the rule:

Activate the changes

Click on Activation > Activate to activate the changes

Verification

Now try accessing the gambling sites from the two client machines.

For guest user:

As one can see, the guest user has been redirected to the response IP we had configured as part of our DNS Control policy for guest users.

For authorized user:

As one can see, the authorized user is able to successfully resolve the IP address for a gambling site, as permitted by our DNS Control policy for authorized users.

According to the documentation trail, all the reasons are listed under the

ietf.org

site.

Here is some web logs documentation:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/nss-feed-output-format-web-logs

In there, there is a link for the

Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason filter

more information

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

For Access Denied as a filter: I looked at some other documentation and found some insights.

This is usually due to when the SNI (Server Name Indication) does not match with the domain name in the certificate when the handshake is performed by Zscaler. It can also occur due to server certificate validation failures or OCSP revocation check failure.

This is an aggregate of all knowledge sources that I can find, it may not be fully accurate. For specifics please reach out to support.

## Softphone network requirements... Does every ZIA customer in the world bypass :5060 and :5061?

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AOGMPhCQP/softphone-network-requirements-does-every-zia-customer-in-the-world-bypass-5060-and-5061
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-04-01T16:15:56.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

Ryan_N

(Customer) asked a question.

March 27, 2024 at 6:11 PM

Softphone network requirements... Does every ZIA customer in the world bypass :5060 and :5061?

Been a while since I checked in here...!

I have provisioned several different softphones through ZIA but I am hitting a wall here with

ServiceTitan Phones Pro

. I don't generally rush into Zscaler Support cases because, in my experience, the focus is always 'how quickly can we bypass this traffic' instead of properly handle it with any of the tools available to us such as URL and Cloud App Control, Firewall Control, etc. This time, I find myself opening a support case and in the support reps defense we did troubleshoot the connectivity and they were also confused as to why my configurations were not working. Unfortunately, I do not have a TAM to communicate with but that's just the way the cookie crumbles for me.

After 2 hours of troubleshooting together, we collected to ZCC packet captures and I provided to the case.

Support suggested that I add "0.0.0.0/0:5060" & "0.0.0.0/0:5061" to destination exclusions at the policy level therefore completely bypassing the SIP requirements for the soft phone network requirements. Prior to bypassing 5060&5061 the only part of the connectivity test that was failing was the Firewall requirements for ports between 16384-32768. After bypassing 5060&5061, I am now failing the SIP requirements of the test as well...

Support also provided this link.

ZIA & Application Layer Gateway Enabled Applications | Zscaler

Protocols that are not supported (like SIP, H.323, H.248, VOIP, and TFTP) should be bypassed from Zscaler by changing the configuration on the firewall or router when configuring your GRE or IPSec tunnel.

To me, that document suggests either of the two options. Zscaler bake the bypass of unsupported protocols into their own application. Or produce a process allowlist of everything that

needs

to be bypassed similar to the below document? Or maybe there is one and I just haven't found it...

Certificate Pinning and SSL Inspection | Zscaler

What I am trying to accomplish seems fairly simple compared to other soft phones... Going to scrap what I have and start from scratch again while waiting for the next support update. Of course, the moment I disable ZIA, the test succeeds in "Firewall Ports" and then fails in VOIP and SIP where it would succeed through ZIA until I bypassed SIP at a policy level.

Phones Pro network recommendations and setup (servicetitan.com)

ServiceTitan Network Test (visualware.com)

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

827 views

(Customer)

Well......

I fixed this by simply stopping SSL inspection to the service titan network tester... Which isn't listed as a requirement anywhere within their documentation.

BUT! I got a working solution to give to a customer and that is all that matters!

Hopefully others see this if they experience similar issues with other soft phone setups.

Thanks,

Ryan

bandwidth drop

, we are currently testing Dynamic Gateway PAC with the following string return: "PROXY ${GATEWAY_FX}:80; PROXY ${SECONDARY_GATEWAY_FX}:80; DIRECT".

So far, there haven't been any major issues. However, we received reports from end users stating that certain websites failed to load or access until redirected using the fixed node "sin4.sme.zscalerthree.net" instead of using load-balanced nodes.

1 answer

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Azwan ArifThe PAC file configuration appears to be correct; however, it would be extremely helpful if we could identify the specific websites that are failing to load. This would allow us to determine whether the issue is rooted in traffic being routed through a specific Data Center or if there is another underlying cause.

For instance, a common scenario is that a website might block connections originating from the Chicago Data Center while allowing traffic from the Singapore Data Center. This situation often arises because certain websites restrict access from specific geographic regions.

To resolve this issue, it’s typically necessary to contact the server team in charge of the website and request that Zscaler’s IP addresses be whitelisted.

However, there are other scenarios but the above is the most common one.

Thank you.

(Partner) asked a question.

April 19, 2024 at 1:20 AM

DNS Traffic Method

Hi Team,

I need some advice about DNS traffic method, in condition ZCC pre login (user didn’t login yet and strict enforcement turned on) what DNS internal traffic method should i applied, it’s bypassed or over tunnel? Because for road warrior we use split tunnel with VPN and user still can access internal application without need to login ZCC

ZIA - Forwarding

1 answer

391 views

Armando

(Employee)

9 months ago

Hi @Masadi Naim​ In this case it depends on your needs. Do you want users to use your internal DNS or do you want users to go through Zscaler's DNS (through the tunnel)?

If the choice is to use your internal DNS, then traffic should be bypassed from the Zscaler cloud, while if traffic should go through Zscaler, in the Mobile Admin portal in the DNS inclusion list, you can use this wildcard "*" to send all traffic though the tunnel.

Thanks.

User15811313291854375697

(Customer) asked a question.

May 1, 2024 at 12:59 PM

Proxy Hostname

In cenr (https://config.zscaler.com/zscaler.net/cenr), what does the "Proxy Hostname" represent for each node?

For example, for Tokyo IV, the Proxy Hostname is tyo4.sme.zscaler.net.

I noticed that when I went to https://ip.zscaler.com/, the Zscaler proxy virtual IP (165.225.110.10) is the same as the actual IP address of tyo4.sme.zscaler.net. So, does this mean that the "Proxy Hostname" is the load balancer within the Zscaler datacenter?

ZIA - Forwarding

4 answers

861 views

Top Rated Answers

Omar

(Customer)

2 years ago

The hostname

tyo4.sme.zscaler.net

resolves to a different IP addresses which indicates use of Dynamic DNS resolution for load balancing and failover, but won't considred it as a load balancer.

You can say it is more of a distributed setup where multiple edge servers (nodes) can handle requests, directing users to an optimal node based on various factors such as load, geographic proximity, and availability.

Typically, the proxy hostname is a generic identifier that resolves to a set of IP addresses specified in the list.

Hope it answers your question😁

Selected as Best

All Answers

Hi,

Omar

(Customer)

2 years ago

You have to setup a NSS logs server (download it from Zscaler portal)

Deploying NSS Virtual Appliances | Zscaler

Connect your Zscaler NSS logs server to your Zscaler ZIA portal

From the ZIA portal configure you logs stream from the Zscaler portal (choose what logs you want to push)

And then just forward them to your SN instance.

Just make sure you parse your logs correctly.

More Details here:

NSS Deployment Guides | Zscaler

## Managing the QUIC Protocol

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ASPQhcCQH/managing-the-quic-protocol
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-09-02T05:47:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - SSL Inspection

Ryan_N

(Customer) asked a question.

May 6, 2024 at 1:34 PM

Managing the QUIC Protocol

Wanting to start this thread and check to see what other Zscaler Internet Acces Customers are doing.

Recently, I have been getting upticks in browser latency reports and I have been able to replicate the experience on multiple workstations where I can generate anywhere of 10-60 seconds between clicks with ZIA enabled. I also noticed a commonality between my traffic and all the users reporting the issue. More QUIC traffic... I am looking for information in Chromium Org where they suggest they are optimizing their QUIC protocol or making changes to how much traffic is pumped through that protocol, but I don't see much.

So, as it is already blocked and I am doing what the

Managing the QUIC Protocol | Zscaler

article says to try first I looked for other options. I noticed we didn't have a policy around QUIC within Intune and I stood up some test policies to disable QUIC at the browser level. This should force revert all the QUIC traffic to standard TCP and then be delivered much better to the end user in the browser. So far that is the experience, and I will be sending all reports this direction so that I can make a planned effort to change this for all soon.

However, Zscaler Support told me to call my ISP... As they commonly do when I can generate Latency or open latency related tickets. This didn't make a lot of sense being that I could replicate the latency on Edge & Chrome, but Firefox was just fine... I find it weird that support always treats me as if we are the only customer in the world that has the latency issues. I wanted to see if any others have been having latency reports for the last 2-3 months this year. I want to say my earliest report was a single user back in January/February time frame, but I have been able to basically classify this as an org wide issue at this point as I measured the "proxy latency" across my organization for a 24hr period and the average latency was 10.63+ seconds rather than milliseconds...

The process I am taking with end users for the time being is below.

Windows Workstation

Chrome Browser

navigate to "chrome://flags"

search for "quic" (experimental quic protocol)

select the drop down that states "default" and select "disabled"

Edge Browser

navigate to "edge://flags"

search for "quic" (experimental quic protocol)

select the drop down that states "default" and select "disabled"

MacOS workstations

open the Terminal from Applications > Utilities folder

enter the below command

defaults write com.google.Chrome LegacyTLSEnforcedNegotiationPolicy -bool true

ZIA - SSL Inspection

6 answers

2.1K views

Celso

and

mathias

like this.

Ben_Garrison

(Employee)

2 years ago

Are you having latency issues outside of the QUIC isolation you described? Because I'm with you, if QUIC is disabled and latency is restored, then not sure why I would need to speak with ISP.

If latency is still happening then yeah sure there may be other factors outside oF QUIC

Ryan_N

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hey Ben,

Once I disable the QUIC flag on the browsers I can basically eliminate that proxy latency that users are experience and confirm that my ZIAFW policy is continuously preventing the QUIC.

It sort of appears like the QUIC protocol isn't necessarily failing back to TCP in our scenario and its just being prevented continuously until the transaction times out or fails.

Thanks,

Ryan

JoeE

(Customer)

2 years ago

We started experiencing the exact same issue in the last few weeks, but reports increased significantly the week of 4/22.  I had a call with our TAM and he noticed a lot of QUIC traffic in packet captures taken while recreating the issue.  We were blocking QUIC in the Default Cloud Firewall policy, but that is just a Block/DROP.   So the browser would just keep trying to send QUIC packets and then at some interval (it seems about 30 seconds), it would fall back to TCP.  He had me create a QUIC specific policy that used Block/ICMP as the action, so that the browser would get a response back and fall back to TCP faster.  This seems to have resolved all our issues.  Now why this just started being an issue we have not determined.

After learning this, it seems the default action for blocking QUIC should be Block/ICMP instead of Block/Drop.

Ryan_N

(Customer)

2 years ago

Interesting...

Your post is the first that made me go back and more granularly read the link.

Managing the QUIC Protocol | Zscaler

The link states to be a "BLOCK/RESET" rule, whereas both yours and my environment are "BLOCK/DROP". Nobody that is on my team recalls configuring this rule originally and that it was likely something pushed out really quick in the initial deployment.

I am now testing "BLOCK/RESET" to see the experience but will keep "BLOCK/ICMP" in mind as well.

Arguably, I really don't see any reason not to disable it on the browsers... Not too sure why we would continue to send the traffic for Zscaler to block it to make it divert back to TCP and support a TCP handshake and SSL inspection. Disabling it at the browser level seems to deliver the best UX so far.

Thanks,

Ryan

Ryan_N

(Customer)

2 years ago

Also, it is hard for us to find an RCA for the recent massive uptick in latency being experienced.

For the users sending standard 80/443 traffic through Zscaler it is

acceptable

to set these users to Z-Tunnel1.0, however any SaaS application requirements you may have configured within ZIA, this will not be an option as 1.0 only supports 80/443 and everything else will go through your perimeter infrastructure or users home networks.

Obviously, you can also allow QUIC, but this is not Zscaler best practice and will break the SSL inspection on all of these transactions.

Something I did to narrow in on Chromium was attempt to use firefox and other browsers that are not managed by Chromium Org. The Latency is gone; however we do not support these other browsers, and Edge + Chrome are the only browsers we make available to our end users...

I would say the closest thing we have been able to determine is that recent CHROMIUM updates are the cause but its hard to pin down to anything specific in their release notes. I know the deprecated support for DTLS1.1 late last year and based on the packet captures that I have generated it no longer looks like QUIC is failing to TCP as it just continuosly sends until the session fails or times out.

Please let me know what else you are able to find and I hope my note is helpful.

FYI, I attempted BLOCK/RESET and BLOCK/ICMP and these options don't seem to help. It isn't until I go to edge/chrome://flags and change the QUIC capability that I can resolve the latency. It seems like the most logical next step as why we would leave the browser in a state where it is promised to block by our #1 ZIAFW rule seems silly if the end result is 10-60 second delays.

Thanks,

Ryan
