## Failed Client SSL Handshake

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000ASQTuBCQX/failed-client-ssl-handshake
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-09-03T12:06:13.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - SSL Inspection

Khue

(Customer) asked a question.

May 8, 2024 at 12:08 PM

Failed Client SSL Handshake

Occasionally, I get an error with a page that has an issue with SSL handshake processing. Typically this manifests itself in the logs as a Policy Action error with the message "Dropped due to failed client SSL handshake". I can enable additional fields in the Web Log viewer like "Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason" however, this information is inadequate to say the least. This leaves my only recourse to create an SSL Bypass rule and I am kind of tired of that being the only solution without a decent reason to justify it. As an example, googleapis.com hosts some content in a core CSS for one of our highly used resources on the web. Again, I got the "Dropped due to failed client SSL handshake" and the only reason I could discern from the "Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason" was "Close Notify or Client TCP Reset". This is not adequate. What was the negotiation error? Was there no ciphers available for client and server to agree upon? If so, state that. Show me the offered ciphers and protocol, show me what the Zscaler cloud accepts. I assume the handshake failure is coming from the negotiation of the connection between the GoogleAPIs.com host and the Zscaler Cloud because if I bypass ZIA, the client connection from browser to GoogleAPIs.com works fine.

How can I help myself out with this besides creating an SSL bypass rule/policy? What SSL/TLS protocols and Cipher suites does the Zscaler Cloud allow/accept to negotiate on? How do I get more information to address issues like this?

ZIA - SSL Inspection

13.22K views

(Customer)

I agree this is a bit cryptic.  I would suggest to open a feature request case to see if the logging could be enhanced to give greater detail.

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hello Khue,

usually this happens due to SSL certificate pinning. There is not much Zscaler can do about this. Checking

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/certificate-pinning-and-ssl-inspection

confirmed this at least for the mentioned .

googleapis.com

-URL, which is listed in the above list. So best practice here is to add (all) the URLs from the help-page to an URL-category-group and exempt this from SSL inspection - at least thats what we did.

It still remains a mystery for several years  now why Zscaler decided to maintain this cert-pinning-list only in the knowledgebase and does not provide any preconfigured URL category here. But thats how it is ;-).

We had no issues since exempt some efforts in ccassionally checking for changes.

BR

Manuel

Khue

(Customer)

2 years ago

I am not sure I agree that this is certificate pinning related in this case after reading the article. The article indicates that the situation happens with applications typically and this particular issue is occurring within browsers. Example being that I am going to

www.domain.com

and in the network dump, I can see that there are resources in a CSS object that stall the page processing and eventually time out. These resources point to googleapis.com. Which according to the logs I do see, are creating the policy action block of "Dropped due to failed client SSL handshake". Additionally, when the Zscaler client is disabled, the page seems to work just fine.

When SSL Inspection is enabled, I am unclear what portion of the connection the errors are referring to. When I see a Policy Action of "Dropped due to failed SSL handshake" and a Client SSL Handshake Failure Reason of "Close Notify or Client TCP Reset" wouldn't that indicate that the connection from Zscaler Cloud Service Edge to

GoogleAPIS.com

is the leg that failed the SSL handshake? Given that this is a simple browser connection it seems unlikely that this is related to Certificate Pinning.

Thoughts?

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Ah, I see your point - sorry, was not aware your issue is browser specific.

Zscalers supported ciphers for ZIA can be found here:

. When checking supported ciphersuites of eg.

storage.googleapis.com

indeed everything looks fine, at least for TLS1.3.

So Pauls recommendation to issue an FR for more details is possibly the best way to go here. In the meantime engineering support should be able to figure out whats going on in your example.

For anyone following this specific issue, this may be related to QUIC. For some reason, it appears that a few of the users in my environment have their browsers attempting to use QUIC protocol over standard TCP HTTP/HTTPS connections. I do not have any reason why. Zscaler support brought this up late in the conversation and I have found the following article that outlines the logic:

Managing the QUIC Protocol | Zscaler

I have implemented a firewall rule as suggested. I will update on the results after I have accumulated more information.

Ramesh Mani

use global ZEN IPs for monitoring. Define static routing of IP1 and IP2  to tunnel 1 and tunnel2.

sus

(Customer)

2 years ago

Keeping your IPSec tunnels healthy is key to secure and reliable network connections. Proactive monitoring helps identify issues before they disrupt traffic.

high-speed internet packages

Techniques like Dead Peer Detection (DPD) ping the other end to confirm its liveness. Additionally, monitoring tools can track tunnel status, data throughput, and encryption key lifespans. Alerts can be set to notify admins of potential problems, allowing them to take corrective action and ensure smooth data flow across the tunnel.

## Atlassian & Zscaler ZIA Best Practices for HTTP2 - Part 1

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AUjnbCCQR/atlassian-zscaler-zia-best-practices-for-http2-part-1
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-06-05T02:30:46.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - SSL Inspection

Nelson

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited June 5, 2024 at 2:30 AM

Atlassian & Zscaler ZIA Best Practices for HTTP2 - Part 1

This article outlines how best to configure Zscaler ZIA in order to provide the best user experience to users of Atlassian products. This document should be used as a companion guide to the

Zscaler and Atlassian Deployment Guide

, which outlines how Zscaler should be deployed with Atlassian for Zscaler ZIA, ZPA and ZPC.

This guide is for network administrators, endpoint / IT administrators, and security analysts responsible for deploying, monitoring, and managing enterprise security systems. For additional product and company resources, refer to:

Zscaler Resources

Atlassian Resources

Appendix A: Requesting Zscaler Support

IP addresses and domains for Atlassian cloud products

Software Versions

This article was authored using ZIA v6.2 (as of May 2024) and Atlassian Production Release, current as of May 2024. An Atlassian free tier account was used to create and verify the features enabled and used as examples. Create an

Atlassian Free Account

. Click Log in, then select Sign up for an account.

Zscaler and HTTP/2

Zscaler supports inspection of HTTP traffic using the

ALPN

protocol (Application-Layer Protocol Negotiation). ALPN is an extension of TLS which allows for negotiation of HTTP connections in the most efficient way. It has now become common for SaaS applications and web servers to offer HTTP/2(as well as HTTP/1.1) as part of the ALPN protocol negotiation to enhance users' experience of web applications.

In 2023, Zscaler added support for

SSL inspection of the HTTP/2 protocol

for web and non web traffic. However, by default, this feature is not enabled by default and must be explicitly enabled by the Zscaler ZIA Administrator through Zscaler support.

If a web server presents HTTP/2 as a connection option, Zscaler ZIA will always choose HTTP/1.1 for that connection with the default settings.

For some web applications, forcing HTTP connections to HTTP/1.1(Instead of HTTP/2) can impact the user experience. Therefore, it is recommended to enable HTTP/2 inspection in order to provide the best user experience.

Configuring Zscaler ZIA SSL Inspection Policy for HTTP/2

If your Zscaler ZIA tenant is not enabled for HTTP/2 inspection, it can be enabled by opening a support ticket and requesting it be enabled. Once HTTP/2 is enabled for your tenant, a selection dialog becomes available in SSL Inspection Policy settings called ‘Enable HTTP/2’:

Policy>SSL Inspection

Edit a new or existing SSL Inspection Policy:

HTTP/2 will need to be enabled for all policies which need it.

Loom Video:

How to enable HTTP/2 in your ZIA tenant

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited June 5, 2024 at 2:33 AM

Atlassian & Zscaler ZIA Best Practices for HTTP2 - Part 2

How best to configure SSL Inspection policy for Atlassian services

In some cases, you may want to be more explicit with your SSL inspection policies. In this case, defining the explicit destinations may be required. Atlassian documents these URLs here:

IP addresses and domains for Atlassian cloud products

. In order to do this for Atlassian you would need to do the following:

Define Atlassian URL’s which need to be defined in policy:

Create a new custom URL Category Administration>URL Categories

Click ‘Add URL Category’

Populate the form as below with the following domains:

.atlassian.net

.atlassian.com

.trello.com

.bitbucket.org

.atl-paas.net

.jira.com

Note:

The preceding ‘.’ is important as it indicates a wildcard for all domains/sub-domains that match.

If you are using custom domains for your Atlassian services, make sure you add them to this list.

You can also add the explicit first party domains from Atlassian that you may be using such as

https://nscaler.atlassian.net

Click Save and navigate to Policy>SSL Inspection

Click Add SSL Inspection Rule and do the following:

Adjust the Rule Order to match your tenant requirements

Specify the rule name

Select the URL Categories dropdown and select the URL Category you created called ‘Atlassian Cloud Service URLs’

Enable the HTTP/2 toggle

Save

Apply and Activate the policy changes, attempt to generate some traffic towards the Atlassian services you are using

How to view logs in Webview and confirm HTTP/2 inspection is taking place

Then navigate the Web Insight logs and create a filter matching:

Current time period

ALPN Protocol: HTTP/2 over TLS

URL Search: Domain matching ‘atlassian’. You should see HTTP/2 transactions

Loom Video:

How to create a specific SSL Policy for Atlassian URLs with HTTP/2

For GRE yes, in our case it was something like

if (URL.search(/

google.com

/) > -1)	return "

PROXY

yourGRE.net

:9443

";

or

if (myLocation == "Chile")		return "PROXY

ChileGRE.net

:9443";

Or a 'catch all' which directed any web request to GRE.

Online PAC tester can help you test the URL using your PAC to see why it's ending up on the firewall.

Maybe it's a typo in the PAC (I've done that) or

non-standard port

which follows default route and ends up on the FW ?

## Zscaler advises to use MFA in ZIA but no MFA option for default admin account

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AW0PHdCQN/zscaler-advises-to-use-mfa-in-zia-but-no-mfa-option-for-default-admin-account

ZIA - Authentication

tower-block

(Customer) asked a question.

June 19, 2024 at 3:12 PM

Zscaler advises to use MFA in ZIA but no MFA option for default admin account

We got a Product Security Advisory from Zscaler yesterday to enable MFA for our ZPA and ZIA admin portal accounts.

Turned on MFA for the default admin in ZPA using TOTP, but I went to do the same in ZIA and there is no option – password only.

How can we follow this advisory if the option doesn't even exist?

ZIA - Authentication

4 answers

546 views

CKAIJA

(Employee)

2 years ago

ZIA is Service Provider initiated Log ins ---- so any MFA you need on the Admin logins can be fully configured at the IdP not in ZIA, you can also once SSO is enabled and enforced for all ADMINs remove the Cloud password for all admins with the exception of the Default system admin that should be kept in a password vault and never used by the Customer ------

Also once set in say Entra ID ----- you can also enforce that the links launch from the Azure portal -- my Enterprise APPs page --- and you can MFA and CAS that all your organization requires

As a mater of Best Practice there should be no more then 3 Super Admins ---- 1 the default never used --- and 2 that are owned by the customer - SSO +MFA only ---- for access all other users should be driven into Role based access and limited in scope and ability to alter policy --- this includes all API access and Partner access

Naman

(Employee)

2 years ago

The issue might be related to how Terraform handles state and updates to existing resources.

You can try to Check the Current State: make sure it correctly reflected via: sh terraform show

Refresh the State: State file may not be synced : sh terraform refresh

Debug Output: Use Terraform's debug output to get more insights into what might be causing the issue:

You can also try below payload :

resource "zia_url_filtering_rules" "default_block" {

name      = "[Terraform] Default block"

order     = 3

state     = "DISABLED"

protocols   = ["ANY_RULE"]

action     = "BLOCK"

url_categories = var.blocked_categories

override_users = null

This might help ensure that the override_users parameter is not being updated implicitly.

kevin.benni

(Partner)

2 years ago

Thanks Naman. For the payload you shared, I tried the same as part of troubleshooting but the problem with that approach is, to set a value for the override_users field the block_override needs to be set as true and the moment you do that in the policy it appears that any user can override the block which is not something I want.

Naman

(Employee)

2 years ago

I have not tried the below payload but i hope that may help you.

It's a refined version of the resource block to ensure block_override remains false and avoids implicit changes to override_users:

resource "zia_url_filtering_rules" "default_block" {

name      = "[Terraform] Default block"

order     = 3

state     = "DISABLED"

protocols   = ["ANY_RULE"]

action     = "BLOCK"

url_categories = var.blocked_categories

dynamic "override" {

for_each = var.block_override ? [1] : []

content {

users = var.override_users

Now we define the var.block_override and var.override_users in the variables file:

variable "block_override" {

description = "Whether to allow block override"

type    = bool

default   = false

variable "override_users" {

description = "List of users allowed to override block"

type    = list(string)

default   = []

This configuration ensures that the override block is only included if block_override is set to true, otherwise, it is excluded from the resource configuration.

This may prevent Terraform from attempting to update the override_users parameter.

2) Depends on your customer config but generally Zscaler recommends using the Windows Light weight Packet filter driver.

Also depending on config they could use you double PAC which was required for wildcard bypasses but not anymore.

3)Several online Pac testers available just to verify the Pac file is correct for your required bypass.

4) Okay

5) Again depends on your customer but from ZCC 4.3 and higher you have the option to configure a Custom Process bypass which could be an easy test.

6)So tunnel 2.0 is all ports and protocols but assume yours is only 443 right ?

No, Zscaler is fully user based and requires idp as Ramesh mentioned.

Understand you don't want to bother the customer but I can only think of these choices:

1) Pac testers to confirm bypass.

2) Zscaler client uses same loopback port as your EXE.

3) Custom Process bypass but your customer needs to create this using a test App Profile which is quick and easy.

4) Is the backend of your App Azure hosted? If so let the customer just add the destination url to custom SSL bypass category as a test.

## Managine QUIC v2! WebView2.dll (embedded browser functionality not respecting browser control)

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AXRTC5CQP/managine-quic-v2-webview2dll-embedded-browser-functionality-not-respecting-browser-control
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-01-23T21:08:59.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Authentication

Ryan_N

(Customer) asked a question.

July 10, 2024 at 7:49 PM

Managine QUIC v2! WebView2.dll (embedded browser functionality not respecting browser control)

Here we go again......!

My last post was around the latency our organization was experiencing on our managed browsers with the QUIC protocol since Chromium updates late last year. We resolved these issues by following

Alternative

method as the initial blocking of QUIC on ZIA-FW was no longer functioning properly. Once we disabled QUIC on the browsers the issues were resolved.

Around the time we disabled QUIC on the browsers we started noticing sporadic latency reports around Teams, Outlook, CyberArk's PSMConnectionMgr.exe Application, and more.

While investigating this latency we did troubleshot extensively and noticed that WebView2.dll was a common factor in all the reports. As WebView2.dll embeds browser functionality into applications it is somewhat difficult to monitor this traffic through ZCC pcaps as the app would fail from Tunnel2.0 to 1.0 and then send all the data as application data. After adding some additional filters to the pcaps we noticed that all the Application Data was piping out UDP/443 traffic (QUIC!!!).

We tested many different configurations around this and there was no resolution identified for the Latency. I opened a case with Zscaler support(

Case Number : 04913822). We did a lot of the same troubleshooting as well as some additional testing with through the escalation process. We(org side) stumbled upon the below documentation and eventually added a regedit key to disable QUIC for WebView2 and resolved countless latency issues with applications.

The part that is troublesome here is our sr management doesn't latch on to org-wide changes that we test, validate, and deploy when there is no official documentation that suggests the change is needed. I have requested through the case that Zscaler update documentation around WebView2.dll and managing the QUIC protocol but they seem very hesitant as "

As we do not have any known or global issue found with webview2 and Microsoft  or CyberArk ." This is a troubling response, if we did not have ZIA we would not have ever needed this control around the QUIC protocol. If we weren't following the doc on managing QUIC protocol by blocking it from the browsers, we likely never would have seen these issues across our org.

I hope this post makes it to other customers experiencing similar latency issues with applications that have WebView2.dll dependencies as we fixed quite a lot when we added the reg key.

Computer\HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Edge

Add Key - WebView2

Add DWORD (32-bit) Value - QuicAllowed - 0x00000000

Enterprise management of WebView2 Runtimes - Microsoft Edge Developer documentation | Microsoft Learn

- Browser policies do not apply to WebView2

Microsoft Edge Browser Policy Documentation | Microsoft Learn

Microsoft Edge WebView2 Policy Documentation | Microsoft Learn

How can you use browser policies within WebView2? · Issue #2507 · MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback (github.com)

Need support for Webview2 browser policies to enable Kerberos delegation · Issue #2974 · MicrosoftEdge/WebView2Feedback (github.com)

Thanks!

ZIA - Authentication

Hi Ryan,

One thing worth checking is whether you have a block/reset  or block/drop rule for QUIC. Block/reset would be recommended as it speeds up the failover from QUIC to older versions of HTTP.  Having a block/drop rule means that the browser might first try QUIC and take quite a while to become aware that QUIC is not available and then failing over to another version. With a block/reset rule the browser will immediately receive a reset package and failover to HTTP after that.

- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-07-17T18:46:58.000Z

kev.whelan

(Customer) asked a question.

July 16, 2024 at 10:53 AM

Custom HTTP Headers or Custom XFF

Is it possible to either set or customise the XFF request header or create a custom header based on a User's location or Active Directory group with ZIA ?

I am trying to mark a Zscaler Enterprise customer's request packets with a secure value (although the external IP address of the customer site - they have many) would be a good start.

Thank you in advance fpr your consideration.

ZIA - Forwarding

7 answers

1.41K views

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

2 years ago

We don't do user/admin customizable header insertion today, though there's probably an enhancement request out there for it.

We DO insert an XFF Header with the IP the ZIA Service Edge receives the traffic from.   In the case of a public ZIA Service Edge, by default we insert an XFF with  the public IP we received the traffic from for road warriors or GRE/IPSec Tunnel traffic).

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

2 years ago

If you would like customer header controls as a feature, you should have your assigned Zscaler SE get an enhancement request submitted with your use case details, etc.

kev.whelan

(Customer)

2 years ago

Thank you so much for your replies.

In the case of traffic sourced from on-prem equipment using the agent, can this be configured to be the egress address of the customer's site? Or is it obfuscated.

I am trying to identify traffic arriving at a site under my control as being sourced from one of my customer's public IP addresses.

If there was some way i could just test this using some bespoke config, that would be fantasti and an enhancement request could be more detailed.

I am assuming that custom headers cannot be inserted at Zscaler prixt egress?

Once again, thank you . I have been trying to work this for some time and your attention is very much appreciated.

Kev

MikeRuiz

(Employee)

2 years ago

When the traffic is proxied nortbound from a public ZIA Service Edge, assuming it's HTTP or Inspected HTTPS, then it is currently getting an XFF Header showing the Public IP NAT address of the site.  If it's HTTPS that's not inspected we can't insert it.

kev.whelan

2 years ago

OK so if the user is on a trusted network and the traffic is not tunneled using the client, the external NAT address of the clients infra will be in the egress xff ?

MikeRuiz

2 years ago

Any inspected http/https traffic that goes through a ZIA Public Service Edge has an XFF inserted with the public IP from which it was received.  It doesn't matter if it was forwarded by the client connector, pac file, GRE/IPSec tunnels, etc.

Not sure what you mean by to extend this "to client traffic on customer networks."  Do you mean if they have a Virtual or Physical ZIA Private Service Edge onsite?

kev.whelan

If inspected, the public IP from which the traffic was received will be in the egress HTTP XFF as per the standard.

## How To: Allow SSH on HTTPS port for specific domains using ZTFW

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AZFzVTCQ1/how-to-allow-ssh-on-https-port-for-specific-domains-using-ztfw
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2025-05-02T16:46:12.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Cloud Firewall

siddhartha.aggarwal

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited July 29, 2024 at 6:25 PM

How To: Allow SSH on HTTPS port for specific domains using ZTFW

In this article we will see how you can use ZTFW to allow SSH traffic destined to HTTPS port (TCP 443) for specific domains only, while still blocking SSH traffic to HTTPS port for other domains.

Pre-requisites

1) Client machine with ZCC/Z-Tunnel 2.0 forwarding all DNS traffic to ZIA Cloud

In this setup we have a client machine with ZCC/Z-Tunnel2.0 with DNS resolver set to a public DNS resolver such as 8.8.8.8:

The DNS resolver is set to a public resolver (such as 8.8.8.8) to ensure that all DNS traffic is sent to ZIA Cloud. This is required because we will use a wildcard FQDN in our FW policy to match the domain for which SSH traffic should be allowed.

As documented at:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/configuring-firewall-filtering-policy

To evaluate wildcard FQDNs against non-web traffic, Zscaler requires the IP address to which the FQDN resolves. Hence, for non-web traffic, the Zscaler service should be aware of the preceding DNS request/response. To ensure this, forward all of your DNS traffic to the Zscaler service if you intend to configure wildcard FQDNs in policies.

2) Appropriate licenses

Here we will be using Advanced FW license.

Step-by-step guide

1) Enable SSH tunneling under ATP

Go to Policy > Web > Security > Advanced Threat Protection:

Set SSH Tunneling to Allow:

2) Enable Enforce Firewall Control option for the location

If the location from where the user will access the ZIA Cloud is defined as a Location, make to enable the Enable Firewall Control option for that location.

Go to Administration > Resources > Traffic Forwarding > Location Management

Click on the location you want to add/edit and enable the Enforce Firewall Control option:

3) Configure FW policy

To configure a FW policy rule, go to Policy > Firewall > Access Control > Firewall Control.

Add the following two rules:

Rule: Add a FW policy rule to allow SSH traffic on HTTPS port for the wildcard FQDN

Network Service: HTTPS

Network Application: SSH

Destination: Wildcard FQDN: .github.com (Note the dot at the beginning of the FQDN).

Action: Allow

Rule: Add a FW policy rule to block SSH traffic on HTTPS port in general

Network Service: HTTPS

Network Application: SSH

Destination: Any

Action: Block/Reset

Here is a summary of the two rules:

Note: Make sure these two rules are above the Recommended Firewall Rule that allows all DNS/HTTP/HTTPS traffic as shown above.

4) Activate the changes

Click on Activation > Activate to make the new changes take effect.

Verification

Access the host ssh.github.com - it should get allowed as per our FW config:

Access a different SSH server on port 443 (here I had provisioned a custom SSH server listening on port 443 for testing purpose) - this should get blocked as per our FW config:

Check the Firewall Insights logs:

Important points to keep in mind

In some case you may see the Action in the log message as "Allow due to insufficient app data". See the following Community article for details:

https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u00009evnDdCAI/when-allow-due-to-insufficient-app-data-log-entry-value-appears-and-when-it-does-not

In the above FW configuration rules, we paired matching on Network Application with another matching condition, Network Service. This is consistent with the recommended best practices as explained at:

https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000A0dGk2CQE/best-practice-for-cfw-rules-with-network-application-dpi-detections-as-condition

## StackHawk with Zscaler SSL Inspection

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AajgvcCQA/stackhawk-with-zscaler-ssl-inspection
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-09-05T15:11:26.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - SSL Inspection

User16182582818315999266

(Customer) asked a question.

August 21, 2024 at 8:06 PM

StackHawk with Zscaler SSL Inspection

We have some devs using StackHawk on both Mac and PC. I was able to get the PC users working by adding the Zscaler root cert to the cacert store it uses on Windows. I haven't been so lucky with the Mac users.

When I use keytool on the mac. it says the cert is already added and when I do the suggested command line from Stackhawk support.

hawk init --outbound-proxy-cacert-path=/Users/user/ca-certs/ZscalerRootCertificate-2048-SHA256.pem --verbose

It returns the error:

Exception in thread "main" Error validating certificate:Unable to verify certificate. The Trust chain for the certificate may not be able to be verified. This could indicate a transparent TLS proxy intercepting the traffic or other Person-In-The-Middle issue. If you need help troubleshooting this issue, please reach out to

support@stackhawk.com

and a wall of java errors.

Does anyone have any suggestions? Everything StackHawk support has mentioned doesn't work. The packet captures don't look like they do cert pinning but temporarily bypassing auth.stackhawk.com may work. Waiting on the developer to get back from PTO to confirm. We don't really like bypassing sites from SSL Inspection if we can help it.

This feels like a stackhawk config issue.

ZIA - SSL Inspection

4 answers

564 views

Top Rated Answers

User16182582818315999266

(Customer)

2 years ago

I was able to figure out the issue finally.

sudo keytool -import -trustcacerts -alias zscalerrootca -file /Users/username/ca-certs/ZscalerRootCertificate-2048-SHA256.pem -keystore /Applications/hawk.app/Contents/runtime/Contents/Home/lib/security/cacerts

You will receive a prompt the cert already exists in the system-wide CA. StackHawk uses its own CA keystore and you will answer yes to this.

The password will be 'changeit'

Selected as Best

All Answers

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AamMyxCQE/use-case-advice-scenario
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-08-29T07:22:14.000Z

ZIA - Authentication

avshch

(Customer) asked a question.

August 27, 2024 at 9:53 PM

Use case advice scenario

Our traffic forwarding method to ZScaler is IPSEC. We are being asked to setup policy which would prevent users from accessing the internet via Zscaler from a web-browser (IoT devices and Windows domain controllers) . At the same time any other processes should be able to access the Internet (DNS, 2FA provider, Windows updates and etc). Could anyone advise on any work around for this use case, except implementing firewall rules? We are considering installing ZCC (for non IoT servers) on a these servers, but not sure if it would interfere with remote access to the servers via MS RDP.

Thanks,

ZIA - Authentication

5 answers

256 views

Omar

(Customer)

2 years ago

It is not recommended to use ZCC on servers.

You can always use Zscaler's Firewall filtering from the admin portal and setup the desired policy without the need to install ZCC on servers.

Instead of ZCC, in Zscaler Locations, create a sub location for servers and your servers Subnet and exclude authentication for them and apply the policies from the Zscaler Firewall.

More details below:

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-firewall-filtering

(Partner)

2 years ago

IPsec won't be possible. Zscaler Client Connector for VDI has different ways of tunneling Point-to-Point (P2P) Tunneling Mode and Any-to-Any (A2A) Tunneling .Mode

You should put your Servers and IoT devices on separate networks.

Create sub-locations in Zscaler and apply different firewall/url filtering policies to each sub-location.

## SIPA forwarding rule options with Standard Zero Trust Firewall

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AbTzr0CQC/sipa-forwarding-rule-options-with-standard-zero-trust-firewall
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-09-25T16:56:33.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

Stefan Sebastian

(Employee) asked a question.

Edited September 10, 2024 at 4:04 AM

SIPA forwarding rule options with Standard Zero Trust Firewall

What is SIPA?

Traffic passing through the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange can egress any Zscaler IP address assigned to any given region in which a Zscaler data center is operating. This anonymizes the traffic in a sense where Zscaler is the source IP address for any given internet destination. The benefit is that "Company A" cannot be distinguished from Zscaler or any other Zscaler customer traffic. The disadvantage is only when certain destinations need to create ACL-based rules which depends on traffic to come from a consistent IP address that represents Company A and only Company A.

Source IP address Anchoring (SIPA) is a feature that allows egress from the Zscaler Zero Trust Exchange from a customer-controlled IP address. This is done by effectively directing certain traffic from Customer A through an App Connector which is controlled by Customer A.

For more information about SIPA, please see the

SIPA Helpdocs

Per-User Forwarding Needs Advanced Zero Trust Firewall

SIPA requires a Forwarding rule. Traffic forwarding is a function of the Firewall.

Standard Firewall includes the ability to define rules based on IP, port, protocol (L3/L4) and by FQDN or wildcard FQDNs including Forwarding rules. The Advanced Firewall brings several additional features but in terms of Forwarding rules it brings the ability to define a rule based on user, group, or department -- basically per-user rules supporting IdP integration.

Most importantly: Without the Advanced Firewall, SIPA Forwarding rules cannot be created in a per-user basis and need to use the policy constructs available to the Standard Firewall

Options for SIPA Forwarding Rules with Standard Firewall

The options for defining SIPA Forwarding rules using the policy constructs of the Standard Firewall include:

Rule by source IP address. Where source means the private 10-space or similar assigned to customer users which are selected as a group or individually into a source IP group then referenced in the forwarding policy;

Rule by destination IP or FQDN. Customer creates either a dest IP object (like the source side above) or a Custom URL (careful, forwarding supports the full URL path and just the FQDN portion). Then reference these objects in Forwarding policy;

Rule by location or sublocation. Carve out the customer users into locations and reference these in Forwarding policy;

Rule by combining any/all of the above. These conditions are logically ANDed together and so all have to match (be "true") for the forwarding rule to hit. A customer Admin can get pretty tightly defined rules by specifying "any flow (from a source IP in 10.1.1.0/24) AND ((is going to example.com) or (2.2.2.2)) AND (is in sublocation3) forwards via SIPA". This is a good way to narrow down options 1, 2, or 3 if any one of them by themselves isn't narrow enough.

Forward rule with Standard ZT Firewall

hm, good question. I think there is no way atm to do this by the report function. Go to web insights - select time frame , apply filter

click overall traffic - select URL host and top 100

In the top right most, click print view

1 like

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

You will only get "transactions" for listed sites by this. But transactions do not necessarily reflect the number how often a site has been called by users in their browsers as one call to a dedicated website usually causes many following "transactions" to this website (e.g. by loading assets or css etc.).

Therefore filtering a csv and removing all "Referrer URL" entries containing the URL in questions will return complete other numbers.

I am able to share this one:

Logs from ZCC:

AppInfo - System and App Info

Setupapi.dev

- Driver/Installation issues

ZSAAuth - Authentication/Login issues

ZSAService - Service/Registry or session related issues.

ZSATray - UI/Interaction or Windows proxy settings.

ZSATunnel - Traffic/Network issues

ZSAUpdate - App update/Auto update issues

And for me were very useful to know that:

ZPHM: Cleanup which is Zscaler Proxy Health Monitoring Cleanup.

And the string in the logs:

INF

notify connectivity change

means that there was a network issue on user end, which leads to the reconnection on Zscaler client side.

I don't know if it is useful for you :)

## PAC File Statements

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AdDE0TCQW/pac-file-statements
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-21T05:35:47.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

sharuk

(Partner) asked a question.

October 18, 2024 at 11:06 PM

PAC File Statements

How the expressions work in the pac when we give the staements.

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, "example.com")) ||

(shExpMatch(host, "example.com")) ||

isInNet(host, "10.0.0.0", "255.0.0.0") ||

IsinNet is user for IP address so that it will check fo the IP. In case of localhost or DoaminIs host and shExpMatch how does it work and how the statements works and how it will check

ZIA - Forwarding

1 answer

472 views

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

2 years ago

localHostOrDomainIs

Evaluates hostname and only returns true if exact hostname match is found.

(localHostOrDomainIs(host, "

example.com

")) - This validated and return true if

example.com

matches as hostname

shExpMatch

Will attempt to match hostname or URL to a specified shell expression, and returns true if matched.

(shExpMatch(host, "

example.com

"))  - Returns true if any requests request for hostname

example.com

or if its files or folder

isInNet

This function evaluates the IP address of a hostname, and if within a specified subnet returns true. If a hostname is passed the function will resolve the hostname to an IP address.

isInNet(host, "10.0.0.0", "255.0.0.0") - Returns true if ip address of the hostname is in this range

myIpAddress()  - This will resolve the Ip address of the host machine and can use as below,

isInNet(myIpAddress(), "10.0.0.0", "255.0.0.0") -  Returns true if the user host machine IP address is this range mentioned.

## Does it require Public IP if using Private VZEN to connect

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AdE8c0CQC/does-it-require-public-ip-if-using-private-vzen-to-connect
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-22T10:28:55.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Forwarding

selva

(Partner) asked a question.

October 22, 2024 at 6:20 AM

Does it require Public IP if using Private VZEN to connect

As per the below link, if customer wants to setup private traffic forwarding using VZEN (hosted either in OnPrem or Cloud).

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/about-virtual-service-edges

Does it require

Public IP

to configure on the Virtual Service Edge servers to connect with the Zscaler cloud?

ZIA - Forwarding

2 answers

230 views

Top Rated Answers

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

2 years ago

If the Private VZEN / Virtual service edge is going to deploy for internal users connects from private network doesn't public IP. The traffic needs to forward to GRE / IPsec or PAC or L2 forwarding.

If your external users wants to connect from public IPs or DCs through internet then Public Ips is needed. Not recommended to such deployment with VZEN. You may go with physical private service edges.

Selected as Best

## Google Chrome does not work with ZScaler.

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AdZtI7CQK/google-chrome-does-not-work-with-zscaler
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-10-31T01:38:27.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - Browser Isolation

mdpaula

(Customer) asked a question.

October 23, 2024 at 1:39 PM

Google Chrome does not work with ZScaler.

Hello everyone! good morning/afternoon!

I am not an expert in your solutions (so I don't if i classified correctly Category and Topic...), but I am bringing this difficulty in Google Chrome here to see if there is any "how to" tip that I can forward to my security team to solve this problem, since we have several questions about problems with Chrome here in Brazil. My understanding is that security software in the context that we have implemented here is causing a lot of difficulty in the user experience, that is, we should be thinking about a security solution to help users and we end up "forcing" them to use personal equipment many times because they cannot execute things in a corporate environment.

I follow this steps but not possible to solve, when I unload ZScaler everything is good.

It sounds frustrating to have Zscaler working on Edge but not on Chrome. Here are some steps you can try to resolve these issues:

Update Chrome

: Ensure that Chrome is updated to the latest version. Sometimes, compatibility issues can be fixed with an update.

Clear Cache and Cookies

: Go to Chrome’s settings and clear the cache and cookies. This can often resolve navigation and performance issues.

Check Proxy Settings

: Make sure the proxy settings in Chrome are correctly configured and match those in Edge. Zscaler might be using different settings for each browser.

Disable Extensions

: Some Chrome extensions might interfere with Zscaler. Try disabling all extensions and see if the problem persists. If it resolves the issue, enable them one by one to identify the culprit.

Authentication Settings

: Verify that the authentication settings in Zscaler are correctly configured for Chrome. Sometimes, different browsers handle authentication differently.

Reinstall Zscaler Client Connector

: If none of the above steps work, try reinstalling the Zscaler Client Connector. This can fix any corrupted installation issues.

Thank you!

(Customer) asked a question.

November 5, 2024 at 2:39 AM

ZIA -  MS Edge browser issues

We're having an issue with ZIA and MS Edge browser. Users are noticing delayed page loading in Edge when connecting to various Microsoft sites via ZIA, such as security.microsoft.com. Chrome works fine, the page loads in roughly 2 seconds, while Edge takes 29 seconds. When we disable ZIA in the client connector, Edge works fine, the page loads in roughly 2 seconds. I am new to Zscaler, so any guidance would be appreciated.

ZIA - URL Filtering

## Request to eliminate ForgiGate Virtual Firewall in Azure

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000Ads9AWCQY/request-to-eliminate-forgigate-virtual-firewall-in-azure
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-11-07T12:15:25.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZWS

allenb090

(Customer) asked a question.

November 6, 2024 at 9:57 AM

Request to eliminate ForgiGate Virtual Firewall in Azure

We want to eliminate the existing deployed FortiGate Virtual Firewall in Azure and want to leverage Zscaler to take it's place and ensure all of our public websites on IIS servers are able to function correctly. Can someone guide me on how to make this possible as with some detailed info.

FYI: We already have deployed ZPA which gives us VPN access to the resources.

ZWS

5 answers

221 views

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hello allenb090,

that won't work. Zscaler does not provide this feature, at least not for websites which should be public available and easily accessible (see also Zscalers "Browser Access"-feature). To replace your FortiGate you will need to leverage Azure Services like AppGw with WAF or Azure Firewall.

BR

Manuel

allenb090

(Customer)

2 years ago

Hi Manuel,

So there’s absolutely no way to protect the Azure Infra with Zscaler or by any of it’s products?

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

It depends how you see "protect Azure Infra". You CAN use Zscaler (e.g. ZPA) to leverage secure access to Azure Services without the need to make your Azure Services visible for the public internet for your internal company employees, assets and ressources. But if you want to protect e.g. your public accessible company website hosted on an Azure VM for lets say OWASP10 vulnerabilities there is no Zscaler product to archieve this - at least none I am aware of.

allenb090

(Customer)

2 years ago

How about the Zscaler Cloud Connector?

manuel

(Customer)

2 years ago

No. Please also check Zscalers help and kb:

Cloud Connectors are virtual machines (VMs) that

simplify traffic forwarding to Zscaler services

. The Cloud Connector also secures s

erver access to the internet

and provides direct connectivity to the Zscaler cloud, providing apps with highly secure and simplified access

to the internet

https://help.zscaler.com/unified/about-cloud-connectors

nabeela.mallick

(Partner) asked a question.

November 11, 2024 at 10:09 AM

How to analyse packet capture logs for ZIA

Hello,

After packet capturing the logs there is folder which get downloaded my question is in that file there are multiple folders so which one we use to analyse the logs so that we can analyse the traffic flow that where the URL is getting blocked or where the issue is arising.

Client Connector

3 answers

1.08K views

Naman

likes this.

Top Rated Answers

Jainil_G

(Employee)

2 years ago

@Nabeela Mallick​ ​ As mentioned by Manuel, you can check the PCAP file. Some of the commonly reviewed log files are listed below:

ZSAAuth: To extract authentication logs

ZSAService: To extract session and registry information

ZSATray: To inspect anything that appears as an error on ZCC

ZSATunnel: To inspect connections to the service edge, Mobile Portal, or any application

The above log files are important that can be reviewed based on issue occurrence date & time, but there are other log files that can also be reviewed depending on the use case.

The below guide can be helpful for the Packet capture file location, and other details.

https://help.zscaler.com/zscaler-client-connector/enabling-packet-capture-zscaler-client-connector

Thanks,

Jainil_G

harry.janakiraman

(Partner) asked a question.

November 18, 2024 at 8:55 PM

Browser Proxy to ZIA

Hello,

I am trying to send traffic from a browser to ZIA using proxy in my windows device. This is unauthenticated traffic. The idea is for any users to use the PC for browsing web but at the same time block adult contents using ZIA.

I have taken the PAC URL from ZIA and applied it to the proxy setting in my PC with Port 80 (Also tried port 443). The IP.Zscaler.com does not go through ZIA.

Is this even a supported feature in Zscaler? Is IPSEC/GRE tunnel a must have to forward traffic to ZIA?

Any ideas please

Thanks

Harry

ZIA - URL Filtering

4 answers

304 views

harry.janakiraman

likes this.

Eugene_Fruman

(Partner)

2 years ago

Hello Harry,

This is a supported method to forward the traffic,  you can read about all the limitations and methods to forward traffic on this page

https://help.zscaler.com/zia/choosing-traffic-forwarding-methods

specifically Pac file for your use case.

In terms of troubleshooting either your browser is not respecting or the pac file is being overwritten by GPO settings generally.

Best.

2 years ago

Thanks Eugene, i have set up the Browser proxy based on the link and the traffic does go via ZIA, (Based on

ip.zscaler.com

). However the policy of blocking a site doesnt work and no logs can be seen.

Ramesh Mani

(Partner)

2 years ago

If you inside the corporate behind any GRE / IPsec; PAC file or proxy IP forwarding will work without authentication.

Whereas if you are outside of GRE / IPSec , then you need to authenticate yourself,  Unauthenticated traffic wont work if you are coming from unknown location.

## Browser Plugins blocking through ZIA

- Source: https://community.zscaler.com/s/question/0D54u0000AeX4qUCQS/browser-plugins-blocking-through-zia
- Type: Q&A
- Last activity: 2024-11-25T05:02:39.000Z
- Note: ユーザー投稿であり Zscaler の公式見解ではない。内容が古い場合があるため投稿日を確認すること。

ZIA - URL Filtering

Subham

(Partner) asked a question.

Edited November 22, 2024 at 4:30 PM

Browser Plugins blocking through ZIA

How can we block specific type of browser plugins through Zscaler

ZIA - URL Filtering

2 answers

1.22K views

joemozdy

(Customer)

2 years ago

You aren't able to block the installation of browser plugins via Zscaler. You can restrict any traffic that these plugins generate though. You an also talk with your support teams who manage your user endpoints to see if there is a way to restrict the installation of browser extensions through administrator policies or something similar.

Jainil_G

(Employee)

2 years ago

Hello @Subham Ghorui​ Proxy plugins and extensions should be restricted from being downloaded and configured on browsers, as they enable users to bypass Zscaler security measures. These extensions allow the browser to ignore the system proxy PAC file.

Hence, Zscaler recommends that users configure a Group Policy Object (GPO) to block the download of plugins or set policies in Google Workspace and Microsoft Edge to prevent the download of extensions.

Kindly the refer the below document for reference

Prevent Users from Installing Extensions on Google Chrome

Use group policies to manage Microsoft Edge extensions

BR

Jainil_G
